new_roles.title: Director, Instrument Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**Position Summary**
====================

The primary purpose of this position is to plan and direct departmental functions (Instrument Manufacturing, Engineering, Instrument Refurbishing) at the St. Louis Operations site to ensure achievement of the corporate goals and objectives of the worldwide bioMerieux organization. This position is responsible for the manufacture and maintenance of instrument production and refurbishment through oversight of multiple teams. In addition, this position: provides technical expertise and quality support through implementation of projects and continuous improvement activities; identifies and justifies projects for capital funding, and deliver the projects on time and budget. Also requires coordinating and overseeing the implementation of engineering projects related to cost improvements and new product introductions, ensuring cooperation within and outside the department at both the local and global levels. And finally, responsible for developing and maintaining an engaged, motivated and skilled production work force.

**Primary Duties**
==================

* Manage Manufacturing – Manage the manufacturing and refurbishment groups to ensure customer satisfaction. Deliver the forecasted product on schedule with no errors or nonconformities. Maintain the complex manufacturing process and minimize loss. Maintain high employee morale, drive cooperation between departments at both local and global levels, and drive employee career development.
* Manage and Maintain Production Equipment – Ensure that the manufacturing areas are maintained so that production can continuously manufacture and refurbish product. End result: Successfully manufacturer product to meet demand and improve efficiency to reduce the COGS.
* Product Transfer – Manage the transfer of new products from Research to Manufacturing. Validate the new processes to meet regulatory requirements and ensure the necessary procedures are in place to order parts / materials to meet market demand. End result: Successful market introduction of new, high quality products that meet all relevant and applicable regulatory requirements.
* CAPA Investigations – Manage and provide technical expertise to projects related to investigating failures in current product production or testing processes.
* Cost Improvement and Risk Management – Manage and provide technical expertise to justify and implement cost improvement projects in Operations.
* Finance – Ensure adherence to Departmental budgets.
* Personnel – hiring, maintenance, organization, engagement, and performance of qualified manufacturing, engineering, and other personnel.
* Perform all work in compliance with company quality procedures and standards.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
==================

* Bachelor’s degree required– Engineering, Supply Chain Management, R&D, Business, or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience leading manufacturing operations, with budget oversight and demonstrated experience in cost reduction and operational efficiency.
* 3+ years experience managing operations in an ISO 13485 regulated manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience leading transformational change.
* Demonstrated experience in talent management and succession planning.
* Experience with capacity, automation, capital investments preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**
====================================

* Consistently upholds and reflects the core ethical principles and values that bioMérieux promotes.
* Comfortable giving clear, direct, and actionable feedback.
* Driving continuous improvement by evaluating processes and implementing necessary changes.
* Inspire and energize individuals to achieve their best performance.
* Drive for Results while successfully removing barriers.
* Communicates instructions clearly and effectively.
* Advanced Microsoft Suite Skills: demonstrates deep knowledge; manages complex tasks and integrates multiple tools independently.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**
================================

* Direct supervision of approximately 1–5 employees.
* Indirect supervision of approximately 100+ employees.
* Required to make financial, manufacturing process, organizational changes, product and team development decisions.

**Working Conditions**
======================

* Domestic travel required: 10% of time
* International travel required: 5% of time
* Total travel: 15%

The estimated salary range for this role is between $155,000-$198,000. This role is eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and individual performance per bioMérieux’s bonus program. This range may differ from ranges offered for similar positions elsewhere in the country given differences in cost of living. Actual compensation within this range is determined based on the successful candidate’s experience and will be presented in writing at the time of the offer.

In addition, bioMérieux offers a competitive Total Rewards package that may include:

* A choice of medical (including prescription), dental, and vision plans providing nationwide coverage and telemedicine options

* Company-Provided Life and Accidental Death Insurance

* Short and Long-Term Disability Insurance

* Retirement Plan including a generous non-discretionary employer contribution and employer match.

* Adoption Assistance

* Wellness Programs

* Employee Assistance Program

* Commuter Benefits

* Various voluntary benefit offerings

* Discount programs

* Parental leaves

new_roles.title: Director, Operational Excellence
new_roles.description:
The Director, Operational Excellence will focus on delivery excellence, process optimization, resource management, and stakeholder management. The Director will be an operational leader who develops frameworks and effective ways of working on which our organization can build in the coming years. This includes ownership of organizational resource tracking, resource planning, hiring process support, and staff augmentation vendor management, so the organization has the right talent in the right roles at the right time in line with funds planning. The Director and team will ensure that the organization develops and fully integrates a continuous improvement culture, with the ultimate goal of ensuring team efficiency, and financial effectiveness.

 

* Leads priorities focused on service delivery and capability alignment, resource management, budget/financial management, vendor and technology management, communications, and training
* Partners with the Leadership Team in short- and long-term planning activities that align with the organization’s strategy, vision, operational plan, and goals
* Establishes and maintains organization-wide resource tracking, providing visibility into headcount, allocation, capacity, utilization, and cost across colleagues and contingent workers
* Leads resource planning in partnership with the Leadership Team and Finance, forecasting demand, identifying capability and capacity gaps, and recommending the right mix of full-time and augmented staff
* Supports hiring processes in partnership with Talent Acquisition and PX, including position requests and approvals, job description development, requisition tracking, interview coordination, and onboarding readiness
* Manages processes related to staff augmentation vendors, including vendor selection, rate and contract negotiation, performance management, and spend oversight
* Drives innovative thinking and planning, leveraging new technologies as needed, to address the needs of the organization and its individual capabilities
* Challenges the status quo and drives continuous improvement by establishing a solid foundation and implementing standard ways of working, systems, processes, and frameworks.
* Works closely with cross-functional peers and team members to consolidate efforts for org processes improvements, but also applies independent decision making to ensure best possible approach is being implemented.
* Promotes a continuous improvement mindset and process improvement initiatives through communication, training, and best practices, ensuring accountability through governance.
* Has critical impact on significant reduction of administrative and redundant tasks across Engineering & Technology organization through applying most efficient and suitable AI tools and bringing in innovative ways of working.
* Builds, develops, and grows relationships with internal and external stakeholders and vendors at every level
* Serves as strategic program/project manager for key organizational projects. Has direct accountability for budget assigned to these projects and management of related vendors, supports oversight processes for organizational budget.
* Coaches, mentors, and supports the professional growth of direct reports. Responsible for efficient resource and funds allocation within the team.

**Basic Qualifications**

Bachelors degree and 8+ years relevant work experience

Strong written and verbal communication skills and interpersonal, collaboration, and facilitation skills

Proven analytical and critical thinking skills, and strong background in process improvement

Practical experience with operational, process improvement, gaining efficiencies and project management methodologies and ability to lead project teams

Ability to multi-task and handle multiple priorities while managing aggressive deadlines

Strong ability for independent decision making while working closely with cross-functional peers

Demonstrated ability to manage/lead complex projects, including resource and budget management for assigned projects

**Preferred Qualifications**

Masters degree in related field

Pharmaceutical or Healthcare industry experience

Practical experience with organization setup processes that include job descriptions creation, managing hiring processes with human resources, sourcing contracted resources.

Project Management Professional (PMP) and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt (LSSBB)

Knowledge of or expertise in Digital product development and/or Design Thinking

Experience driving change in a global, matrixed organization

Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

**NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS**

National and International travel may be necessary

Work Location Assignment: Hybrid

Last Date to Apply for Job: 11/30/2026

 
The annual base salary for this position ranges from $176,600.00 to $294,300.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. 
This role is posted in multiple locations. If you are applying for the role in an secondary job posting location where pay transparency regulations apply, your Talent Advisor will share the local pay information with you during the first interview.

Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility.

**Sunshine Act**

Pfizer reports payments and other transfers of value to health care providers as required by federal and state transparency laws and implementing regulations. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. Therefore, if you are a licensed physician who incurs recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Pfizer that we pay or reimburse, your name, address and the amount of payments made currently will be reported to the government. If you have questions regarding this matter, please do not hesitate to contact your Talent Acquisition representative.

**EEO & Employment Eligibility**

Pfizer is committed to equal opportunity in the terms and conditions of employment for all employees and job applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability or veteran status. Pfizer also complies with all applicable national, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act and IRCA. Pfizer is an E-Verify employer. This position requires permanent work authorization in the United States.

Pfizer endeavors to make www.pfizer.com/careers accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding the accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process and/or interviewing, please email disabilityrecruitment@pfizer.com. This is to be used solely for accommodation requests with respect to the accessibility of our website, online application process and/or interviewing. Requests for any other reason will not be returned.

To learn more about acceptable and prohibited uses of AI during the recruitment process, please review our candidate AI-use guidelines available on Pfizer Careers.

new_roles.title: Director, Operations and Infrastructure in Stead, NV
new_roles.description:
The University of Nevada, Reno (UNR) appreciates your interest in employment at our growing institution. We want your application process to go smoothly and quickly. Final applications must be submitted prior to the close of the recruitment.

 

If you need assistance or have questions regarding the application process, please contact our recruitment helpline at (775) 784-1495 or jobs@unr.edu .

**Job Description**

The Department of Physics at the University of Nevada, Reno seeks applications for a Director of Operations and Infrastructure position. The position will support the growth and development of the Applied Sciences Institute for National Security (ASI), **located at the SAGE facility in Stead, NV.**

 

The Director of Operations and Infrastructure provides strategic and operational leadership for the Institute’s administrative and financial, facilities and infrastructure, and safety and security functions. The position is responsible for ensuring that the Institute’s personnel, facilities, financial resources, information systems, and operational practices effectively support its research, education, and workforce-development missions.

 

The Director of Operations and Infrastructure serves as the Institute’s principal operational liaison with University Facilities Services and other university offices on the development of new research capabilities, modernization of infrastructure, and maintenance of the Institute’s facilities and key experimental systems. The position represents the Institute in operational discussions with university leadership, government agencies, national laboratories, sponsors, contractors, and other external partners.

 

The Director of Operations and Infrastructure is also responsible for the safe and secure working practices within the facilities, ensuring staff are creating and following appropriate procedures, students are being trained appropriately and following procedures, and the facility and experimental capabilities meet or exceed requirements for safe and secure operating conditions.

 

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree and five (5) years of related professional experience **OR**

Master’s degree and three (3) years of related professional experience.

**Related Work Experience** : Progressively responsible leadership overseeing complex operations, multidisciplinary teams, budgets and contracts, facilities and infrastructure, safety and risk management, compliance, and collaboration with senior leadership and external stakeholders or related experience.

 

**Schedule or Travel Requirements**

Occasional travel and weekends/evenings to support events or deadlines.

 

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience leading operations in a research laboratory environment.
* Experience developing and implementing safe work practices for hazardous facilities and research activities.
Experience addressing security requirements and export control considerations in a research or technical environment. 

 

**Compensation Grade**

Administrative Faculty – C

Typical salary range for this position is $102,589 (Mid Q2) to $122,576.

 

Candidates will be hired at the level that is comparable to their experience, knowledge, skills and abilities. To view the salary schedule for this position, please visit: Salary Schedules and select Administrative Faculty by Grade. Salary is competitive and commensurate with related education and experience.

 

**Remarkable Retirement**

Our retirement plan is beyond compare. Your 19.25% contribution is generously matched by the University. With the faculty retirement plan, you are 100% vested your first day. Sit back and watch your retirement dollars grow! All permanent employees on an annual "A" or "B" contract who are employed at least 50% full-time are eligible to participate in the NSHE retirement program unless they are members of PERS of Nevada.

**Perks of Working at UNR**

* Health insurance options including dental and vision - Health Insurance
* Generous annual and sick leave and life insurance – Faculty Benefits
* E. L. Wiegand Fitness Center offers annual or semester memberships and spouse/domestic partner membership options. E.L. Wiegand Fitness Center
* Reno is proud to be a University town! Many local businesses offer discounts to WolfCard holders
* Mountain EAP supports employees (and eligible dependents) through life's difficult moments. Mountain EAP is located in Reno and specializes in counseling and advising services for personal or interpersonal issues.
* Faculty Senate is the principal representing body for faculty. Its membership includes representatives from each academic and administrative major unit of the University. Faculty Senate
No state income tax! 

**Grants-in-Aid for Faculty Employees**

The University is proud to provide a reduced-rate tuition benefit to faculty and qualified dependents. Faculty can take up to six credits per semester at a reduced rate. Dependents of faculty have unlimited credits, but in order to be eligible children must be unmarried and under the age of 24 and must receive at least 50% of their financial support from the employee and/or employee’s spouse or domestic partner. Faculty Grants-in-Aid

**Faculty Dual Career Assistance Program**

The University of Nevada, Reno recognizes the importance of addressing dual-career couples’ professional needs. We offer a dual career assistance program to newly hired faculty spouses/partners that provides resources and assists them to identify career opportunities in Northern Nevada. Dual Career Assistance Program

 

**Department Information**

The Department of Physics at the University of Nevada, Reno manages the SAGE facility, located only 11 miles north of the main campus. SAGE is a 182,000 sq ft. cold war era building that is home to an assemblage of unique research laboratories built to create and explore extreme material states. The research program is growing rapidly, with numerous projects from DOE and DoW sponsors, supporting a significant expansion of student research activities, all with a focus on supporting a transition into impactful careers. Please see here for more information: https://www.unr.edu/physics

 

**Contact Information**

Beth Jacobsen at 775-682-8787 or jacobsenb@unr.edu

**Exempt**

Yes

**Full-Time Equivalent**

100.0%

**Required Attachment(s)**

Please note, once you submit your application the only attachment/s viewable to you will be the attachment/s to the resume/CV section of the application. Any additional required attachment/s to the cover letter, references, additional documents sections of the application, will not be viewable to you after you submit your application. All uploaded attachment/s will be on the application for the committee to review. To request updates to attachments, prior to the committee review of applications, please contact the candidate helpdesk at jobs@unr.edu .

**Please attach the following documents to your application:**

1) Resume/CV

2) Cover Letter

3) Contact Information for Three Professional References

 

**Posting Close Time**

This posting will close at 12:00 am on the date listed below. The posting will no longer be available to apply to after 11:59 pm the day prior.

**Posting Close Date**

12/20/2026

Note to Applicant

A background check will be conducted on the candidate(s) selected for hire.

HR will attempt to verify academic credentials upon receipt of hiring documents. If the academic credentials cannot be verified, HR will notify the faculty member that an official transcript of their highest degree must be submitted within thirty days of the faculty member’s first day of employment.

References will be contacted at the appropriate phase of the recruitment process.

Applicants hired on a federal contract may be subject to E-Verify.

As part of the hiring process, applicants for positions in the Nevada System of Higher Education may be required to demonstrate the ability to perform job-related tasks.

For positions that require driving, evidence of a valid driver's license will be required at the time of employment and as a condition of continued employment.

Schedules are subject to change based on organizational needs.

The University of Nevada, Reno is committed to providing a place of work and learning free of discrimination on the basis of a person’s age (40 or older), disability, whether actual or perceived by others (including service-connected disabilities), gender (including pregnancy related conditions), military status or military obligations, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, national origin, race (including hair texture and protected hairstyles such as natural hairstyles, afros, bantu knots, curls, braids, locks and twists), color, or religion (protected classes).

**About Us**

The University of Nevada, Reno is a leading public research university committed to the promise of a future powered by knowledge. Founded in 1874 as Nevada’s original land-grant university, the University serves more than 23,000 undergraduate and graduate students from all 50 states and 63 countries.

Classified by the Carnegie® Classification of Institutions of Higher Education as an R1 (“Very High Research”) university, it is also recognized in the Carnegie® Community Engagement classification. The University is also ranked by U.S. News & World Report among the “Best National Universities” and “Best National Public Universities.” It also ranks in the top tier of the WSJ/Times Higher Education World University Rankings and the New York Times’ “Top Colleges for Economic Diversity.”

Since 2009, nearly $1 billion has been has invested in advanced labs, facilities, and residence halls on the main campus. The University is home to Nevada’s first medical school – the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine and the Wayne L. Prim Campus at Lake Tahoe, where education, research, and creative work thrive in a stunning mountain setting. The University delivers on its original land-grant mission with outreach across the state through the University of Nevada, Reno Extension, Nevada Agricultural Experiment Station, Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology, Nevada Small Business Development Center, the Nevada Seismological Laboratory, and Wolf Pack Athletics.

The main campus is in Reno, Nevada, a burgeoning global technology hub with a vibrant midtown and downtown. Found where the high desert of the Great Basin meets the High Sierra and Lake Tahoe, the beautiful, 290-acre main campus is also a Nevada State Arboretum. The University’s physical infrastructure is expanding with ongoing construction of the newly named John Tullock Business Building, set to open in fall 2025. Groundbreaking is also planned for a new State Public Health Laboratory Building on campus, alongside the recent acquisition of 16 parcels near campus, known as “University Village,” to provide affordable housing for graduate students and early career faculty.

Collaborating with world-renowned organizations, the University fosters innovation through initiatives such as the Digital Wolf Pack partnership with Apple, which ensures equitable access to technology for students, providing new incoming freshman or transfer students with an iPad Air and accessories. Google’s TechWise initiate is an 18-month program that fully supports undergraduate students in becoming entry-level software engineers by graduation.

In 2023, the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Economic Development Administration (EDA) announced that Nevada – led by the University of Nevada, Reno – was named one of the inaugural 31 Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs (TechHubs). Nevada was selected from a competitive pool of 489 applicants from across the United States and its territories. Nevada’s Tech Hub will strengthen America’s lithium batteries, critical elements and other electric vehicle materials industry sectors within the state.

Through its commitment to high-impact education, world-improving research and creative activity, and outreach that’s transforming Nevada’s communities and businesses, the University continues its 150-year tradition of benefitting our state, nation and world.

The University recognizes that diversity promotes excellence in education and research. The inclusive and engaged community on campus recognizes the added value that students, faculty, and staff from different backgrounds bring to the educational experience.

Today, the University delivers on its original land-grant mission of access to education and knowledge by investing in the academics, facilities, support, engagement and vibrant campus life that promote our diverse students’ cognitive growth and academic achievement – all while remaining one of the best values in American higher education.

For more information, please visit the University’s website .

**University of Nevada, Reno**
------------------------------

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Private Markets Operations & Experience
new_roles.description:
**About You**

* Strategic Operator: You excel at translating complex investment strategies into actionable plans, scalable processes, and consistent execution.
* Collaborative Leader: You build strong relationships across teams, advisors, and external partners, creating alignment and accountability while delivering an exceptional client experience.
* Proactive Problem-Solver: You anticipate challenges, navigate complex fund operations with confidence, and bring sound judgment, attention to detail, and a solutions-oriented mindset to everything you do.

 

**The Role**

We’re looking for a strategic, results-driven professional to join our Private Markets team as Senior Director, Private Markets Operations & Experience. In this role, you’ll lead the operational execution of NorthRock’s private investment programs, overseeing fund formation, ongoing administration, program launches, and the advisor and client experience. As a key partner to the Executive Director, Private Capital Markets, you’ll help build the infrastructure, technology, service-provider relationships, and team capabilities needed to support continued growth. The ideal candidate thrives in a collaborative, evolving environment and is known for operational excellence, proactive leadership, and the ability to turn complex strategies into seamless execution.

 

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead end-to-end fund formation and launch activities, including legal entity formation, fund documentation, subscription materials, approvals, and operational readiness.
* Oversee ongoing private fund operations, coordinating subscription processing, capital activity, reporting, filings, and administrative requirements throughout the fund lifecycle.
* Partner with investment managers, fund administrators, legal counsel, tax professionals, and other service providers to ensure accurate, timely execution.
* Anticipate and resolve complex operational challenges, including rejected investment orders, subscription exceptions, and documentation or approval issues.
* Translate fund governing documents and investment program requirements into clear workflows, timelines, responsibilities, and operating procedures.
* Lead the rollout of private investment programs, partnering with advisor teams to develop communications, presentations, educational materials, and client engagement initiatives.
* Enhance the advisor and client experience by identifying opportunities to simplify processes, improve communications, and deliver consistent, high-quality service.
* Serve as a strategic operating partner to the Executive Director, aligning cross-functional teams, managing priorities, and ensuring accountability for key deliverables.
* Evaluate and implement technology solutions, operating systems, and service-provider partnerships that strengthen efficiency and support business growth.
* Help build and develop the private markets operations team, providing leadership, coaching, and guidance to support a scalable operating model.

 

**What You Bring**

* Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration, economics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
* 8–10 years of progressive experience in private markets operations, fund administration, or a related financial services function.
* Direct, hands-on experience forming and operating private investment funds, including private equity, private credit, or private real estate vehicles.
* Comprehensive understanding of the private fund lifecycle, including fund formation, subscriptions, investment operations, administration, and wind-down requirements.
* Experience interpreting fund governing documents and translating complex operational requirements into practical processes and execution plans.
* Proven ability to manage relationships with investment partners, fund administrators, legal counsel, tax professionals, and other external service providers.
* Demonstrated success resolving complex fund operational issues and leading cross-functional initiatives in a growing organization.
* Strong project management, organizational, and analytical skills, with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.
* Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to simplify complex investment information for advisors, clients, and internal stakeholders.
* Experience developing teams, coaching colleagues, and implementing process and technology improvements that enhance operational efficiency.
* Sound judgment, professionalism, discretion, and a commitment to delivering an exceptional advisor and client experience.
* Must be authorized to work in the United States.
* Successful completion of a credit and criminal background check is required.

 

**Compensation & Benefits**

The estimated base salary range for this role is $183,000 – $251,000 per year. Compensation is based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and geographical work location.

 

**About NorthRock Partners**

At NorthRock Partners, we help people reach their potential through impactful advice. Our Personal Office® model delivers integrated financial and lifestyle guidance tailored to each client’s unique goals.

 

NorthRock Partners is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

 

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodation throughout the application and employment process. For assistance, contact PeopleTeam@NorthRockPartners.com.

new_roles.title: Head of Operational Excellence
new_roles.description:
**Overview:** 
 
Vanguard is building an enterprise Operational Excellence capability to strengthen end-to-end process ownership, improve efficiency, and embed continuous improvement across the organization. This newly created, highly visible role will serve as the architect and builder of that capability. Reporting directly to a senior enterprise leader, the Senior Director will establish and scale Vanguard’s enterprise Operational Excellence management system, creating the strategy, operating model, process taxonomy, standards, methods, governance, tools, training, measures, and operating rhythms that enable business leaders to own and continuously improve their end-to-end processes.

The central capability will enable the businesses rather than execute improvement on their behalf. Success will require deep Operational Excellence expertise, enterprise-level operating model design, executive presence, and the ability to translate a technically rigorous discipline into a clear and compelling business imperative.

**What You Will Do:**

* Architect the enterprise Operational Excellence strategy and management system, including the operating model, governance, process taxonomy, decision rights, standards, methods, and management routines.
* Establish a federated model that clearly defines what the central team owns and what business-area leaders own, reinforcing accountability for process performance and sustained improvement.
* Create an enterprise framework for critical and high-risk processes, clarifying end-to-end ownership, expected outcomes, escalation paths, and review cadences.
* Build a common measurement system for process health, including definitions, benchmarks, performance indicators, executive dashboards, and business-area drill-downs that support transparent decision-making.
* Embed disciplined Lean Six Sigma and DMAIC practices, root-cause analysis, process redesign, simplification, and continuous improvement across a large, complex organization.
* Build and lead a new Operational Excellence organization, expected initially to include approximately 8 to 10 professionals, and define the capabilities, roles, talent strategy, and development model needed to scale.
* Partner with senior leaders across business, risk, technology, data, finance, and other enterprise functions to identify systemic issues and translate them into an integrated improvement portfolio.
* Influence prioritization and investment decisions using evidence, balancing client value, risk reduction, productivity, resilience, controls, strategic importance, and long-term enterprise value.
* Integrate existing transformation, risk, control, and process-improvement efforts into a coherent enterprise approach that builds on current foundations rather than creating a disconnected program.
* Build enterprise capability through standards, training, coaching, benchmarking, and practical tools, including the thoughtful use of automation, data, process mining, and AI-enabled approaches.
* Provide decision-ready insights and recommendations to senior officer audiences, Senior Staff, and the Board on process health, progress, emerging themes, dependencies, and investment needs.
* Create clarity, momentum, and followership by articulating what Operational Excellence means for Vanguard, why it matters, and what leaders and teams must do differently.

**What It Takes:**

* At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in Operational Excellence, enterprise transformation, business operations, process excellence, quality, or a related discipline, including leadership of complex, cross-functional initiatives.
* Undergraduate degree or equivalent combination of training and experience. A graduate degree or relevant Operational Excellence certification is preferred.
* Deep expertise in Lean Six Sigma, DMAIC, continuous improvement, process redesign, root-cause analysis, process measurement, and quality or process-management systems.
* Master Black Belt certification or equivalent depth of practical expertise strongly preferred. The successful candidate must be capable of establishing the methodology, not simply sponsoring work performed by others.
* Demonstrated success designing, launching, or materially transforming an enterprise-scale Operational Excellence capability, center of excellence, management system, or federated process-management model.
* Proven ability to move beyond individual projects and create common standards, tools, governance, accountability, and adoption across multiple businesses or functions.
* Experience building a function, team, or capability from the ground up, including organization design, talent selection, capability building, and resource prioritization.
* Executive presence and communication skills, with a record of influencing highly senior leaders, translating technical concepts into business language, navigating resistance, and creating followership without relying solely on formal authority.
* A results orientation supported by quantifiable improvements in efficiency, cycle time, quality, defects, cost, operational risk, controls, client outcomes, automation, or sustained process performance.
* Strong business, risk, data, and technology acumen, with the judgment to connect process health and improvement priorities to enterprise value.

**Special Factors**

**Sponsorship**

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

**How We Work**

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

new_roles.title: Operations Director
new_roles.description:
**Aveanna Healthcare is growing!**

**We are seeking a Home Health Operations Director to join our team, based in Englewood, Colorado.**

**Salary: $82-85K/YR +** **Quarterly Incentive Potential up to 20% of salary dependent on office success**

**Why Choose Aveanna?**

* Health, Dental, Vision Insurance

* 401(k) Savings Plan with Employer Matching
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Company-Paid Life Insurance
* Paid Holidays, Paid Vacation Days, Paid Sick Days
* Easy access to state-of-the-art technology for electronic charting during point of care 24/7 Team Support for direct clinical and scheduling assistance

* Cell phone and mileage reimbursement
* Room for growth and advancement

Position Overview 
The Operations Director (hereafter referred to as “OD”) is responsible for managing and overseeing leadership and administrative functions of an Aveanna location. The OD collaborates with cross-functional teams including operations, clinical and business development ensuring annual business growth, patient care outcomes and financial objectives are met or exceeded. 
 
Serving as the leader of their respective branch team, the OD offers a dynamic work environment where individuals can contribute their expertise in either clinical or non-clinical capacities. The OD embodies Aveanna’s Core Values by building and strengthening relationships with patients, families, field staff, and referral sources while serving as an advocate and trusted mentor for their location team. The OD possesses strong written and verbal communication skills and assures the adoption of all branch-level processes and training standards. The OD ensures their location fully adheres to all Federal and State regulations governing home care agencies. 
 
Essential Job Functions 
Lead, develop, and support a high-performing team by recruiting qualified staff, ensuring timely performance evaluations, establishing and monitoring goals, promoting employee development, and maintaining consistent communication with supervisors and area/regional leadership. 
Build and strengthen relationships with patients, families, caregivers, referral partners, and business development teams by supporting effective introductions, periodic patient home visits, referral source assessments, satisfaction survey follow-up, and growth-oriented partnership objectives. 
Drive branch growth and operational performance by planning and implementing effective growth strategies. 
Successfully address the referral pipeline with urgency, and monitors referral management, admissions and start-of-care timelines. 
Oversee caregiver staffing, productivity, reporting deadlines, and overall service delivery. 
Manage financial and business performance by interpreting financial statements, activity reports, and other performance data; monitoring revenue, billing, collections, productivity, and expense control. 
Identify opportunities for cost mitigation and process improvement. 
Identify operational barriers, implement solutions that improve efficiency and branch outcomes, and partner with area and regional leadership to align priorities with business goals and organizational initiatives. 
Ensure operational readiness and compliance by maintaining adherence to company policies, payor requirements, and applicable federal and state regulations; 
Partner with clinical and operational leaders to address quality concerns; implement corrective actions and support continuous improvement. 
Monitor branch performance indicators to identify trends, mitigate risk, improve patient, caregiver, and business outcomes, and promote a culture of accountability, compliance, service excellence, and operational readiness. 
 
Requirements 
Minimum of an associate’s degree or equivalent work experience in a related field. 
2-3 years’ management experience. 
Satisfies all state requirements, including background checks and any applicable required work authorization. 
 
Other Skills/Abilities 
Must be able to adhere to confidentiality standards and professional boundaries at all times. 
Ability to comfortably work in homes of families with limited resources. 
Quick-thinking and astute decision-making skills. 
Attention to detail. 
Time Management. 
Effective problem-solving and conflict resolution. 
Excellent organization and communication skills. 
Ability to remain calm and professional in stressful situations. 
Strong commitment to clinical excellence. 
 
Leadership skills 
Ability to train and supervise staff. 
 
Preferences 
4-Year College Degree preferred. 
Healthcare and/or pediatric home care experience a plus. 
 
Physical Requirements 
Must be able to speak, write, read and understand English. 
Must be able to travel as needed. 
Occasional lifting, carrying, pushing and pulling of 50 pounds. 
Prolonged walking, standing, bending, kneeling, reaching, twisting. 
Must be able to sit and climb stairs. 
Must have visual and hearing acuity. 
Must have strong sense of smell and touch. 
 
Environment 
Must be able to function in a wide variety of environments which may involve exposure to allergens and other various conditions. 
 
Other Duties 
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. 
 
**Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis for this role and can be submitted by applying to this job posting or by visiting our career page at:** **| Aveanna Healthcare Careers**

As an employer accepting Medicare and Medicaid funds, employees must comply with all health-related requirements in all relevant jurisdictions, including required vaccinations and testing, subject to exemptions for medical or religious reasons as appropriate.

new_roles.description:
Job Description
 
 
Director, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Strategy & Operations
 
 
Position Description
 
 
The Director, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Strategy & Operations is a key leadership role responsible for shaping and advancing the strategic and operational priorities of the U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Business Unit.
 
Reporting directly to the SVP, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases, this individual will serve as a strategic thought partner to the SVP and Leadership Team, translating business strategy into action, driving alignment across priorities, and enabling disciplined execution. The role requires a strong balance of strategic thinking, operational excellence, influence, and change leadership, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, connect across the organization, and accelerate progress against the BU's most important priorities.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities:** 

* Lead the BU strategic planning and operating process, including annual priority setting, Trimester planning and tracking, and ongoing assessment of progress against key objectives.
* Partner with the SVP and Leadership Team to translate strategy into action, identifying priorities, surfacing opportunities and risks, and driving alignment and accountability across the organization.
* Lead high-priority, cross-functional initiatives that advance BU strategy, transformation, and organizational capabilities, including evolving commercial capabilities, new ways of working, AI, and other emerging business priorities.
* Drive leadership effectiveness and decision-making by shaping and facilitating Leadership Team meetings, leader forums, strategic planning sessions, and other key business forums that enable alignment and action.
* Shape BU communications and engagement strategy, ensuring business priorities, strategic direction, and key messages are translated into clear and compelling communications across the organization, including Town Halls and other leadership forums.
* Partner with Leadership Team sponsors to advance talent, culture, and organizational priorities, including Talent & Culture working groups, employee development initiatives, and efforts to strengthen organizational capability and engagement.
* Partner across key financial planning processes, including forecasting, Profit Plan, and investor relations connecting strategic priorities with financial considerations and partnering across Finance and business stakeholders to enable informed decision-making.
* Identify opportunities to strengthen BU effectiveness, simplify ways of working, build organizational capabilities, and accelerate execution of strategic priorities.

**Required Experience:** 

* Bachelor's degree required.
* Minimum of 5 years of experience in marketing, sales, market access, strategy and operations, marketing support, within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
* Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities, including the ability to assess complex business challenges, identify strategic choices, and develop clear recommendations.
* Proven ability to influence and lead without direct authority across complex, matrixed organizations.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders, with the courage to challenge thinking, bring an independent point of view, and constructively navigate differing perspectives.
* Ability to navigate ambiguity and evolving priorities, quickly create structure from white space, and move work forward with sound judgment and learning agility.
* Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing demands, maintain focus on the highest-impact work, and align teams around clear priorities.
* Ability to inspire, motivate, mentor, and align others around a shared vision and clear priorities, with or without direct reporting relationships.
* Strong balance of strategic orientation and operational discipline, with the ability to move seamlessly between long-term priorities and near-term execution.
* Demonstrated ability to connect insights and priorities across functions and levels of the organization, bringing an enterprise perspective while maintaining focus on BU objectives.

**Preferred Experience and Skills:** 

* Vaccines and/or Infectious Diseases experience.
* Experience supporting or leading strategy and operations within a complex commercial organization.
* Experience leading enterprise or cross-functional transformation, capability-building, or change initiatives.

**Required Skills:** 
Accountability, Active Listening, Adaptability, Business Alignment, Business Operations, Data-Driven Decision Making, Developing Proposals, Influencing Without Authority, Influential Leadership, Market Access, Marketing, Market Research, Oncology Marketing, Pharmaceutical Industry, Pharmaceutics, Relationship Building, Results-Oriented, Sound Judgment, Strategic Planning, Strategic Recommendations, Strategic Thinking, Vaccinology

new_roles.title: Sr. Director Operations
new_roles.description:
**What makes DHL great?** Our People! We know each employee’s individual contributions make us the #1 Express Delivery and Logistics Company in the world.

***Distinguished as No. 1 World’s Best Workplace™ by Great Place to Work and Fortune Magazine***

DHL Express is committed to maintaining an environment that empowers every team member to make the greatest possible impact on our business. Our culture is about personal commitment – to our business, to each other and to our global communities. DHL is dedicated to being a great place to work. In addition to competitive compensation packages, our employees enjoy a range of programs, services and benefits that bring the best to their personal lives.

**Start YOUR career with DHL today…**

The **Sr. Director Operations** is responsible for providing strategic input and leading the implementation of the Courier and Pick-up & Delivery strategy. This role ensures the safe, secure, timely, and accurate transportation and delivery of mail, parcels, small packages, and legal documents between locations, in alignment with business objectives, operational requirements, corporate guidelines, and policies.

**Key Accountabilities:**

* Provide input to develop Couriers, Pick-up & Delivery operations strategy to deliver effective collection, transportation, and delivery of parcels while maintaining exceptional service quality and customer satisfaction.
* Plan, organize and control preparation of annual business plans, operational budgets, workforce planning, and resource allocation for delivery operations.
* Provide expertise, coaching, and leadership to frontline managers and supervisors to ensure execution of daily operational activities, achievement of performance targets, and development of future leaders.
* Manage and control service point operations to enable efficient collection, handling, and distribution of shipments while maintaining compliance with operational standards.
* Manage and control scheduling of transportation capacity, traffic volumes, route structures, and delivery resources to maximize productivity and service performance.
* Lead a workforce of more than 1,000 employees across multiple facilities, fostering a culture of accountability, engagement, safety, and operational excellence.
* Demonstrate strong knowledge and experience operating in unionized environments, including labor relations, contract interpretation, grievance resolution, workforce planning, and effective collaboration with union leadership.
* Oversee large independent contractor (IC) networks and transportation providers, ensuring contractual compliance, operational performance, cost management, and service reliability.
* Drive operational expense (OPEX) management through disciplined financial oversight, productivity initiatives, route optimization, and continuous improvement programs to achieve profitability objectives.
* Partner closely with Network Operations, Gateway Operations, Brokerage, Customs, Aviation, and Commercial teams to ensure seamless execution of customer commitments and network requirements.
* Deploy structured approaches to manage operational procedures including shipment processing, sorting, loading/unloading, documentation, scanning compliance, manifests, secure handling, and custody control.
* Implement reporting standards, performance metrics, and operational dashboards to provide visibility into service performance, cost drivers, productivity, and customer experience measures.
* Anticipate changes in customer demand, economic conditions, labor markets, and transportation trends to proactively adjust operational strategies and resource requirements.
* Identify opportunities to improve transportation, delivery, and customer service solutions through process redesign, technology implementation, and network optimization.
* Monitor operational performance and implement continuous improvement initiatives focused on service quality, productivity, safety, employee engagement, and cost control.
* Lead multiple delivery bases and service centers across geographically diverse markets, ensuring consistent execution of operational standards and business objectives.
* Champion safety, security, and compliance programs while maintaining adherence to company policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
* Build strong relationships with key customers, local business leaders, and internal stakeholders to support growth initiatives and enhance the overall customer experience.
* Drive organizational change initiatives, workforce transformation efforts, and strategic projects across the region while maintaining high levels of employee engagement and operational performance.

**Skills/Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree required.
* 8+ years of experience in operations and leadership roles.
* Demonstrated experience in budgetary management and financial accountability.
* Strong background in business and operations management, including managing complex operational environments.
* Experience leading courier, Pick-up & Delivery, dock, and transportation operations.
* Proven ability to lead change management and operational improvement initiatives.
* Strong strategic planning and execution capabilities.
* Demonstrated experience in stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration.
* Proven leadership experience managing a department or business unit comprising multiple teams, including Managers and/or Team Leaders.
* Strong ability to lead, develop, and influence leaders and teams to achieve business and operational objectives.
* Experience establishing priorities, managing resources, and driving performance across multiple operational functions.
* Demonstrated ability to drive employee engagement, foster an inclusive and high-performing culture, and develop strategies that strengthen employee experience, retention, and organizational effectiveness.

**Employee Benefits & Incentives**

DHL Express benefits and incentive offerings are designed to reflect a substantial experience for both employees and their dependents during their career and life journey. The specifics will vary, but wherever you join and in whatever role, you'll find our benefits and rewards are among the best in the industry They include:

* Competitive Pay - Salary Range New Jersey $187,950- $250,600
* Bonus/Incentive Programs
* Retirement Savings – 401K with company match
* Medical, Dental, Vision, well-being programs
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Generous Paid Time Off – Starting at 4 Weeks (PT/FT)
* Paid Leave
* Employee Discount Program
* Employee Assistance & Work Life Program
* Outstanding training opportunities

new_roles.title: LSA Director of Facilities & Operations
new_roles.description:
**How to Apply**
----------------

A cover letter is required for consideration for this position and should be attached as the first page of your resume. The cover letter should address your specific interest in the position and outline skills and experience that directly relate to this position.

**Job Summary**
---------------

**Institutional Context and Operational Scale**

The University of Michigan serves the public through preeminence in creating, communicating, preserving, and applying knowledge, art, and academic values. As the university's largest academic unit, the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts offers more than 100 degree programs across more than 75 academic units and departments.

To support this expansive academic mission, LSA Facilities and Operations (LSA FO) manages a physical footprint encompassing approximately 2,000,000 square feet of building space. This comprises 27 primary buildings distributed across the Ann Arbor central campus, in addition to three outlying academic camps and several leased properties.

**Responsibilities\***
----------------------

**Scope of Responsibilities and Capital Oversight**

The Director of Facilities and Operations serves as a senior administrative leader and strategic advisor for LSA's physical environment, capital strategy, and operational services. Reporting to the Chief Financial and Operating Officer, the successful candidate would lead a 30-person team, including capital project managers, interior designers, facilities coordinators, building managers, movers, sustainability and lab safety team members, and administrative and financial support staff.

This role will lead LSA's transformational capital expansion, a multi-building project featuring new construction and major facility modernizations anticipated to exceed $1 billion in capital costs. The role oversees an annual departmental operating budget of $2 million and directs $20+ million in ongoing annual renovations, expansions, and modernizations. Concurrent responsibilities include:

* **Exemplary Customer Service:** Establish a proactive, service-oriented culture across all facilities operations, partnering with academic and administrative departments to evaluate evolving space and operational needs and implement continuous process improvements that optimize cost efficiency across college assets.
* **Capital Improvement and Renovation Oversight:** Direct all LSA facility renovation efforts, including capital improvement initiatives, specialized laboratory modernizations, interior design projects, and general building construction.
* **Research Infrastructure, Safety, and Support Operations:** Manage the start-up, commissioning, maintenance, and safe operations of core research facilities serving the broader university community, as well as provide administrative direction to the college moving and support services team.
* **Fiscal Stewardship and Sustainability:** Oversee the college utilities budget, lead energy conservation and sustainability initiatives, and manage commercial rental space procurement and lease administration.
* **University Partnerships:** Maintain active collaborative partnerships with university central units, including (but not limited to) the Provost's Office, Facilities & Operations (maintenance services, custodial services, and environmental health and safety), and the Department of Public Safety and Security (DPSS).
* **Emergency Management and Space Planning:** In partnership with DPSS and college academic and administrative leaders, lead LSA's emergency preparedness and crisis management response.
* **Strategic Alignment:** Advise executive leadership on strategic space allocation and long-range capital projects. Translate institutional vision into operational execution and ensure facilities strategies support broader college objectives.
* **Staff Leadership and Development:** Provide strategic leadership, mentorship, and professional development for LSA Facilities and Operations staff. Build a collaborative, inclusive, and accountable team culture that empowers employees, develops future leaders, recognizes individual contributions, and supports continued growth and excellence in service delivery.
* **Workplace Culture and Work-Life Balance:** Cultivate a positive, inclusive workplace environment that recognizes employee contributions and promotes a healthy balance between work and personal life.

**Required and Desired Qualifications**

Candidates for the Director of Facilities and Operations role are evaluated based on a combination of academic credentials, progressive managerial experience, and demonstrated technical competency in complex, decentralized institutional settings.

**Required Qualifications\***
-----------------------------

* A Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, or Business (or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience),
* Ten (10) or more years of progressive responsibility, including direct management of a large department within a decentralized environment of comparable size and complexity.
* Demonstrated experience managing teams of ten (10) or more employees, alongside a record of long-term creative leadership of high-performing teams and comprehensive employee relations oversight.
* Demonstrated ability to build consensus and drive outcomes within a highly decentralized, shared-governance environment, representing the interests of academic leaders while coordinating closely with central institutional authorities.
* Proven success in initiating and executing organizational change initiatives across complex institutions serving diverse stakeholder interests.
* Demonstrated ability to lead large-scale capital projects and/or strategic and innovative facility initiatives aligned with institutional priorities.
* Proven ability to fulfill operational and financial stewardship targets in technical operational environments, alongside experience in emergency management and crisis response.

**Desired Qualifications\***
----------------------------

* A Master's degree or higher in architecture, engineering, business, or a related administrative field.
* Experience in public higher education and academic research environments.
* Five (5) or more years of experience managing technical operations, including capital construction management, space and master planning, core/recharge facility management, and technical contractor oversight.

**Modes of Work**
-----------------

Positions that are eligible for hybrid or mobile/remote work mode are at the discretion of the hiring department. Work agreements are reviewed annually at a minimum and are subject to change at any time, and for any reason, throughout the course of employment. Learn more about the work modes.

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

The target salary range is $180,000 - $209,000. Compensation above this range may be considered for candidates with evidence of exceeding role expectations and driving measurable, enterprise impact, keeping internal equity in mind.

As one of the world's great liberal arts and sciences colleges, LSA pushes the boundaries of what is understood about the human experience and the natural world, and we foster the next generation of rigorous and empathetic thinkers, creators, and contributors to the state of Michigan, the nation, and the world.

 

To learn more about LSA's Mission, Vision and Values, please visit lsa.umich.edu/strategicvision.

 

**Mission Statement**

 

The mission of the University of Michigan is to serve the people of Michigan and the world through preeminence in creating, communicating, preserving and applying knowledge, art, and academic values, and in developing leaders and citizens who will challenge the present and enrich the future.

**Background Screening**
------------------------

The University of Michigan conducts background checks on all job candidates upon acceptance of a contingent offer and may use a third party administrator to conduct background checks. Background checks are performed in compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

**Application Deadline**
------------------------

Job openings are posted for a minimum of seven calendar days. The review and selection process may begin as early as the eighth day after posting. This opening may be removed from posting boards and filled any time after the minimum posting period has ended.

**U-M EEO Statement**
---------------------

The University of Michigan is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

identity_held_roles.title: Director, Sourcing and Production, Robert Graham (Menswear)
identity_held_roles.description:
**About Us**
Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the ha rd work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.
 
 
**Product Development**
From sourcing raw material s to manufacturing, order placement, pricing, quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production/product development team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results-driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.
 
 
**Specific Responsibilities Would Include**
The Director, Sourcing and Product Development reports to the VP of Production for Robert Graham/Saks and will drive seasonal product initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams, including Production, Design, Sales, and Overseas Offices, to develop and execute assigned product lines. The role primarily focuses on apparel development, with additional responsibility for trims and packaging across Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue Private Label.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and manage all aspects of the product development process, from concept and inspiration through quality assurance of finished goods to the end customer.
* Establish shared qualities and fabrics between Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue to ensure alignment across brands.
* Partner closely with overseas hubs and vendor teams to ensure understanding of departmental objectives and leverage vendor capabilities to drive initiatives that expand competencies as needed.
* Analyze product costs, identifying opportunities and collaborating cross-functionally to create solutions through product engineering that maximize product value while accounting for cost impact.
* Oversee cross-functional milestone performance; communicate risks, deadlines, and business impacts when deliverables are at risk.
* Lead vendor sourcing initiatives aligned with driving innovation and service within the overall sourcing strategy.
* Manage new vendor onboarding and ensure all internal partners are connected and prepared to support production needs.
* Facilitate vendor meetings to review in-season development, production, and delivery challenges, and drive solutions.
* Identify business risks and opportunities, escalate appropriately, and propose actionable recommendations for improvement.
* Collaborate closely with Design and Merchandising on product creation from concept to execution, utilizing budget and SKU plans.
* Create and maintain comprehensive material and product libraries with detailed product attributes and testing documentation.

**Our Best Fit Candidate Would Have**

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); advanced Adobe, Photoshop and Illustrator skills required
* SAP experience preferred
* Excellent organizational, written, and verbal communication skills
* Strong team orientation and ability to work cross-functionally
* Ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
* High attention to detail and accuracy
* Knowledge of garment manufacturing, construction, and fabrication

Salary Range: $125,000 - $145,000
 
 
At Centric Brands, we believe our people are our greatest asset, and we seek to structure competitive compensation offers to ensure that we are able to attract and retain the best talent. Our job postings include an annual base salary range at the time of employment. The stated base salary range represents our good faith estimate as to what candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on several factors, including the selected candidate's educational and professional experience, industry knowledge, location, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the selection process. Base salary is a part of a total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, annual bonus and other Centric Brands sponsored benefit programs.
 
 
**Be part of our growing community by getting involved with groups, teams and initiatives like Be Green, Be Giving, and Be Celebrated.**
**Centric Brands is an Equal Opportunity Employer**
Please note that Centric Brands will only reach out to interview, make an offer of employment or conduct onboarding activities for candidates who have applied through our careers site. When interviewing for a position, the candidate experience will include live interaction, such as a video conference or telephone call, with a Recruiter and/or company employee(s). We will never ask for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process. Be aware of suspicious recruitment activity. If you think you are a victim of an employment scam, you may contact your local law enforcement agency and/or visit the Federal Trade Commission website here: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams .
