identity_held_roles.title: Quality Improvement Director
identity_held_roles.description:
***POSITION PURPOSE:***

The Director of Quality Improvement operates under the leadership and direction of the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) and Chief Operating Officer (COO). The CMO maintains direct clinical oversight of clinical quality improvement activities and regulatory quality programs. The Director of Quality Improvement provides organization-wide leadership for EVCHC's quality improvement program. The Director establishes the quality strategy in partnership with executive, clinical, operational and compliance leaders; converts organizational goals and regulatory requirements into measurable work plans; and leads improvement efforts that strengthen patient outcomes, safety, access, equity and care experience. The Director is accountable for reliable quality data, required clinical quality reporting, continuous improvement methods, Patient Centered Medical Home recognition, and the performance of the Quality Improvement Department.

 

***MAJOR POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES AND FUNCTIONS:***

**Quality Strategy and Governance**

* Lead the development, implementation and annual evaluation of EVCHC's organization-wide Quality Improvement and Quality Assurance Plan in alignment with the strategic plan, clinical standards and applicable Health Center Program requirements.

* Establish annual quality priorities, measures, targets, owners and timelines with executive and clinical leadership. Monitor progress and recommend corrective action when performance does not meet established goals.

* Lead or support the Quality Improvement Committee and related workgroups. Prepare agendas, dashboards, meeting materials, decisions and follow-up reports for executive leadership and the Board of Directors, as requested.

* Advise executive leaders on emerging quality risks, performance trends, resource needs and opportunities to improve care delivery across sites and service lines.

* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, patient safety and learning throughout the organization.

**Department Leadership**

* Direct the work of the Quality Improvement Department, including recruitment, onboarding, supervision, coaching, performance evaluation, workload assignment and staff development.

* Develop departmental goals, staffing plans, procedures and budgets that support timely completion of quality priorities and reporting obligations.

* Set clear expectations for the accuracy, timeliness and usability of analyses, audits, reports and improvement support provided by the department.

* Build effective working relationships with clinical care teams, Operations, Information Technology, Compliance, Human Resources, Finance, Behavioral Health, Dental and other departments involved in quality outcomes.

**Quality Measurement and Reporting**

* Oversee the collection, validation, analysis and submission of clinical quality measures and required reports, including Uniform Data System measures, population health platforms transition and readiness, HEDIS and payer measures, grant measures and internal quality indicators.

* Develop and maintain executive, provider, site and service-line dashboards that show current performance, trends, disparities, targets and improvement actions.

* Track provider and care-team performance, identify variation and care gaps, and provide leaders with actionable information while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data-use standards.

* Establish data-validation controls and documentation so that quality reports can be reconciled to source systems and used as an organization-wide source of truth. Partnering with Director of Data and IT operations for oversight on data governance committee.

* Present quality findings in clear written and verbal reports to the Board, executive leadership, managers, providers, staff, health plans and external reviewers, as appropriate.

**Performance Improvement**

* Lead Plan Do Study Act cycles, root-cause analyses and other structured improvement methods from problem definition through implementation, evaluation and sustainment.

* Partner with clinical and operational leaders to improve preventive care, chronic disease outcomes, access, continuity, patient experience, care coordination, documentation and other priority measures.

* Translate data findings into practical workflow changes, training, decision support, audit tools and accountability processes that can be sustained across sites.

* Evaluate improvement results, identify lessons learned and spread effective practices to other care teams, programs or locations when appropriate **Regulatory Readiness and Patient Safety**

* Lead the quality components of Patient Centered Medical Home recognition and renewal, including evidence collection, workflow assessment, documentation, staff education and sustainment of recognized practices alongside Director of compliance.

* Partner with Compliance Director, Risk Management, clinical leadership and Operations on quality-related readiness for HRSA operational site visits, FTCA deeming and risk-management activities, health plan audits, accreditation reviews and other external assessments.

* Support corrective action plans with the Director of Compliance arising from audits, quality reviews, safety events or regulatory findings. Define measures, monitor completion and verify that corrective actions are effective and sustained.

* Analyze trends in patient safety events, grievances and quality-of-care concerns with the appropriate leaders while protecting confidentiality and following reporting requirements.

* Maintain organized records of quality plans, committee actions, reports, audits, improvement projects and supporting evidence required for oversight and external review.

**Clinical Analytics and Health Information Technology**

* Direct the clinical analytics program and define reporting requirements that support clinical decision-making, population health management and performance improvement.

* Partner with Information Technology and system vendors to improve data extraction, interfaces, registries, care guidelines, clinical decision support, templates and reporting tools used for quality measurement.

* Lead data-governance practices for quality information, including measure definitions, ownership, validation, access, change control and resolution of reporting discrepancies.

* Assess the quality and workflow impact of new digital tools and automation used in clinical or quality processes and recommend safeguards, testing and performance monitoring before broad implementation.

* Recommend redesign of workflows affected by the electronic health record, patient portal, population health platforms and other clinical information systems.

**Organizational Responsibilities**

* Participate in executive, management, clinical and staff meetings related to quality priorities and organizational performance.

* Maintain current knowledge of FQHC quality requirements, clinical quality measures, health plan expectations and recognized improvement practices.

* Protect patient, employee and organizational information and comply with HIPAA, confidentiality, cybersecurity and records-management requirements.

* Perform other job-related duties as assigned within the scope of the position.

***POSITION REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:***

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in public health, health care administration, nursing, health sciences, informatics or a related field is required. A master's degree is preferred.

* At least five years of progressive experience in health care quality improvement, population health, clinical analytics or health care program management is required, including at least three years of supervisory or department leadership experience.

* Experience in a Federally Qualified Health Center, community health center or other safety-net setting is strongly preferred.

* Experience leading cross-functional improvement projects and preparing quality reports for executives, governing boards, health plans or regulatory agencies is required.

* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality, Lean or Six Sigma certification, or comparable quality-improvement training is preferred.

**Knowledge and Skills**

* Working knowledge of continuous quality improvement methods, patient safety practices, clinical quality measurement, health equity and population health management.

* Knowledge of HRSA Health Center Program expectations, Uniform Data System reporting, HEDIS measures, Patient Centered Medical Home standards and payer quality programs is strongly preferred.

* Advanced ability to collect, validate, analyze and present health care data and to translate findings into operational decisions and improvement plans.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint and experience using electronic health records, population health platforms, data visualization tools or clinical reporting applications. Experience with NextGen or comparable systems is preferred.

* Strong leadership, project management, facilitation, written communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build accountability across departments .

* Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet reporting deadlines, exercise sound judgment and communicate sensitive performance information professionally.

* Demonstrated commitment to serving medically underserved communities and reducing disparities in access, care and health outcomes.

***WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL/MENTAL ABILITIES AND PROCESSES:***

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

 

* Work is performed primarily in an office and health center environment and requires regular travel among EVCHC sites and occasional travel to meetings or trainings.

identity_held_roles.title: Sr. Director, Additive Manufacturing Systems Engineering
identity_held_roles.description:
**Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future**
======================================

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**Why This Role Exists**
------------------------

Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. The hard problem is not any single machine, material, or line of code. It is making all of them behave as one system. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue.

The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive.

The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* **Architect the system.** Define and control the end-to-end architecture for additive at Hadrian: requirements, interfaces, data model, and acceptance criteria that hold across multiple equipment platforms, modalities, and sites. Treat the factory as the product.
* **Build the digital backbone.** Connect additive equipment, peripherals, and inspection assets to Opus with the same discipline a semiconductor fab applies to connecting tools to the host: standardized state models, telemetry, event streams, and data contracts, with security and configuration control built in.
* **Fuse the sensors.** Bring in-situ monitoring, machine telemetry, environmental data, and downstream inspection into one correlated record per part, then move from monitoring to data-driven release and, where it is justified, closed-loop control.
* **Automate where it pays.** Lead automation across additive cells (material and powder handling, build changeover, part removal and depowdering, post-processing flow, robotics, controls, and safety) with a written case for each: safety, repeatability, and data capture first; labor second. Never automate an unstable process.
* **Lead the three functions as one.** Set standards, priorities, and cadence for materials and process, hardware, and software engineering. Resolve conflicts between them at the architecture level, not the escalation level.
* **Own the applications engineering interface.** With the Head of Applications Engineering, define what a production-ready hand-off looks like, publish the process capability and design-rule data applications engineers build to, and close the loop from floor results back into design guidance.
* **Industrialize the equipment.** Through the hardware engineering leader, own factory and site acceptance, commissioning, reliability (preventive maintenance, spares, MTBF/MTTR), and configuration-controlled modification and upgrade of additive systems, and lead the technical relationships with equipment partners that unlock deeper integration. The machine-level depth lives in that team; the standards and the outcomes live here.
* **Design for the factory.** Partner with Factory Development and Factory Automation on cell and site design: material flow, capacity, simulation, utilities, and the path to lights-out operation for additive.
* **Build quality in.** Make the system itself the evidence: traceability, data integrity, and process control that stand up to AS9100 audits and customer qualification without a separate paper trail.
* **Be the additive voice in Hadrian’s platform.** Carry additive requirements into Core Engineering and the Opus roadmap, and bring platform capability back to the floor.
* **Hire, develop, and retain.** Build a leadership bench under you, set a high technical bar, and make Hadrian the place the best additive systems engineers in the country want to work.

**What We’re Looking For**
--------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a physical science; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
* 12+ years in advanced manufacturing, with real depth in at least three of these six domains: factory design and industrial automation; semiconductor or other high-reliability capital-equipment engineering; manufacturing software and data systems; materials science and process engineering; quality systems in regulated industries; sensing, process monitoring, and sensor fusion.
* 5+ years leading engineering teams, including leading through managers and building at least one function from the ground up.
* Production experience with metal laser powder bed fusion, as a user of the equipment, a developer of it, or both.
* Has led the integration of complex equipment into factory-level software (manufacturing execution, equipment host, or data platforms), including requirements, interface standards, and acceptance criteria.
* Has taken at least one production automation or capital-equipment program (robotic cells, material handling, or equipment with safety systems and controls) from concept through commissioning in a regulated environment (aerospace and defense, semiconductor, medical, or similar), and has owned the reliability of production equipment afterward.
* Fluent across the stack: can review a process flow, a data schema, a metallurgical cross-section, and a controls narrative in the same meeting, and knows which one is lying.
* Has worked as a true peer to a customer-facing or design function, with a record of building clean interfaces rather than absorbing the other team.
* Willing to travel up to 20%, including to Hadrian sites and international partners. Must meet the ITAR requirements below.

**What Will Set You Apart**
---------------------------

* Ph.D. in materials science, mechanical engineering, systems engineering or a related discipline.
* Semiconductor capital-equipment background: equipment-to-host integration, tool matching, fleet data, fault detection and statistical process control at scale.
* Equipment-maker experience developing or launching metal additive systems (new product introduction, cost-productivity trades, design reviews) in addition to user-side experience.
* In-situ monitoring and sensor fusion implemented in production, with data-driven release or closed-loop control.
* Factory design: material flow planning, discrete-event simulation, and highly automated or lights-out operations.
* AS9100 and customer qualification pathways; familiarity with AM specifications (ASTM F42, ISO/ASTM 529xx, SAE AMS 7xxx series).
* Budget or P&L ownership of a capital-intensive program, with a record of making the build-versus-buy and automate-versus-wait calls well.
* Modern software fluency: APIs, event streaming, OT/IT architecture, industrial interoperability standards (OPC UA, MTConnect), and cloud data platforms.

**Compensation**
----------------

For this role, the target salary range is $300,000 - $350,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

**Benefits for Full-time Employees**
------------------------------------

* Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees
 
 401k
* Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.
* Flexible vacation policy
* Equity

**ITAR Requirements**
---------------------

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

**Use of AI in hiring**
-----------------------

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy.

**Consideration of Criminal History**
-------------------------------------

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

**Hadrian Is An Equal Opportunity Employer**
--------------------------------------------

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

Compensation Range: $300K - $350K

identity_held_roles.description:
**Position Overview:**

As the Regional Senior Manager of Post Production/IQR, you will have the unique opportunity to partner closely with several different teams at multiple sites (including IC leadership, reconditioning, and support teams) to drive the strategy behind the development and deployment of Post Production & Quality programs, as well as manage continued performance of internal and external vendors. We are looking for a resourceful self-starter who will set the tone for the successful and fast-paced growth of our Inspection Centers. The Regional Senior Manager of Post Production/IQR role will be heavily focused on leading our teams to effectively close operational gaps and establishing standardized practices that will drive exceptional quality.

**What you'll be doing:**

* Creating and successfully executing large-scale change management initiatives and new process rollouts.
* Other duties as assigned.

* Experience working in a Lean Manufacturing environment
* Experience developing effective and scalable operating systems and processes
* Proven track record of production process improvement and innovation

* Proven track record of leading and developing others

* Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.

identity_held_roles.title: Director Quality & Compliance
identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.** 
 
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

The role offers the opportunity to influence the quality standard for a growing federal business and help prepare the organization to support additional federal programs over time.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

 

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

 

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) facility and meaningful pharmaceutical distribution, logistics or 3PL quality exposure.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

 

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.
Direct leadership of quality teams 

 
 

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

 

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.
* Flexibility to support audits, client needs or quality events outside standard business hours when required.

Eligibility Requirement: This position is open only to U.S. citizens due to applicable federal requirements. By applying, you confirm that you are a U.S. citizen and can provide acceptable documentation verifying your status if selected. 
 
If you are not a U.S. citizen, please do not apply for this role.

Cart.com is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Operations
identity_held_roles.description:
Western Veterinary Partners is seeking a Director of Operations (DO) to lead a portfolio of veterinary hospitals in Florida. The ideal candidate for this role is someone who has successfully managed multiple locations (ideally 10+) in a healthcare, veterinary or multi-site setting. Our ideal candidate is a strong general manager with a goal-oriented attitude, a passion for training and team development, and the business, financial, and strategic acumen to help scale a rapidly growing business and team.

**Market Area to include the following geographies: Orlando South to Miami, including Southwest Florida.**

**Preferred Home Base:** Central Florida

In partnership with the Vice President of Operations and Senior Director of Operations, the chosen candidate will focus on supporting veterinary practices in achieving operational excellence, building culture, recruiting and retaining veterinarians, technicians, and support staff. The Director of Operations will spend extensive time in the field with hospital leadership and staff and be responsible for supporting the overall operations of 8 - 12 general practice veterinary hospitals.

About us:

Western Veterinary Partners (WVP) is a mission-driven company based in Denver, CO. We are driven by our values of integrity, alignment, support, collaboration, growth and relationships. WVP is a private equity backed company that acquires, invests in, and supports animal hospitals throughout the United States. WVP is a highly acquisitive company focused on continued growth and expansion into new markets and states. Post-acquisition, WVP supports its partner practices with the non-clinical side of the business. Our local and collaborative support provides veterinarians with attractive operational benefits of a larger group while maintaining the clinical autonomy and local practice identity.

Job Responsibilities:

Leadership and Culture

* Develop strong relationship with DVMs to assist with recruiting, training, and retention to drive overall business growth
* Achieve results through influence and partnership versus through authority or directives
* Maintain regular communication with doctors and office staff to review practice trends and performance objectives
* Champion WVP's culture and develop teams and leaders through coaching, mentorship, and programs that deliver on the strategic mission
* Provide oversight and support to practice level managers and administrative staff, as well as regional managers
* Instill a sense of accountability and service excellence with our teams at all levels
* Identify opportunities to improve and maintain site-level employee engagement
* Facilitate connections and community among individuals and hospitals within markets and the region
* Develop collaborative and productive relationships across the organization
* Contribute to growth and innovation across WVP by supporting other geographies and organization-wide initiatives

Financial and Business Objectives

* Understand business drivers and create opportunities to optimize them, with a strong focus on volume growth, service mix and offerings, pricing, and margin improvement
* Set, manage and exceed WVP's financial objectives in partnership with sites, regional leaders, and the executive team, with an eye toward future growth opportunities for the company
* Provide overall P&L management for the business, along with a vision for near and long-term value creation
* Partner with hospital leaders, field operators and functional support to diagnose issues, identify opportunities, and develop corresponding action plans
* Employ structured and repeatable management processes with hospital leadership teams to drive operational effectiveness and growth
* Prioritize areas of focus based on impact and urgency; help team do the same

Growth and Strategy

* Assist in the timely and accurate onboarding and integration of recently affiliated veterinary practices while minimizing disruption to the existing business
* Partner with WVP departments (marketing, recruiting, HR, business development, and finance and accounting) to create and implement plans that support business growth, including scheduling optimization, client growth and retention, identification of new services, recruitment of new DVMs, and expansion of existing sites and their capacity
* Partner with hospitals to manage DVM capacity, identify and schedule relief, and plan for succession
* Nurture and elevate innovation and growth ideas to build tangible, scalable programs
* Develop capital budgets for new site development, expansions, and capital equipment purchases, and build and monitor ROI analyses to support business decisions and growth
* Forecast future business needs and develop comprehensive strategic plans at the hospital, market, and region levels

Required Criteria:

* 50% travel
* 5+ years of multi-site operational and/or management experience in fast-growth healthcare services businesses, including previous experience managing a business of similar size and complexity. Previous veterinary experience a plus
* Ability to analyze and assess complex and ambiguous data to make recommendations for strategic and operational improvements, leveraging tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, and Tableau
* P&L responsibility and experience with budget management, personnel management, and team building
* Strong active listening and written and verbal communication skills; Executive presence
* Ability to implement processes in collaboration with the VP of Operations to ensure company objectives are met
* Highly organized and detail-oriented work ethic
* Ability to work collaboratively with all team members, both at the practice level and at the corporate level
* Self-directed and able to work independently
* Bachelor's degree required, master's degree (MBA) highly preferred
* Willingness to spend time in the field visiting and supporting affiliated veterinary practices (approximately 70% of time). Occasional travel to Denver and other company activities

The application window will be open for the next two weeks ending 12/42026. This opportunity will remain online based on business needs which may be before or after the two-week window.

* This role is not open to receiving agency candidates and any contingent submissions will not be honored.

#LI-CH1

Western Veterinary Partners is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, pregnancy, childbirth or related conditions, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Western Veterinary Partners is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in the job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact hr@westernvetpartners.com. Hiring decisions will be based on merit, qualifications and the legitimate needs of the business.

existing_roles.title: Vice President, Global GMP Quality
existing_roles.description:
**MISSION**

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases. We are passionate about advancing scientific discoveries to become important medicines for rare disease patients. We are collaborative, creative, and experienced professionals and we’re looking to augment our team with other individuals who embody our values: care, be real, get it done, and have fun, seriously.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The VP, Global GMP Quality position will be responsible for leading the GMP quality functional teams at Mirum and its subsidiaries (US and International). This position will play a pivotal role in steering the organization toward an ongoing commitment to quality improvement, driving efforts to identify areas for optimization, innovation, and excellence. This person will be responsible for managing, mentoring and supporting a GMP Operations team of clinical and commercial Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) professionals. This person will provide leadership and hands-on support to ensure the seamless execution of GMP QA and QC functions, including product quality complaint investigation, root-cause investigations, and the reporting of critical GMP issues to executive management.  This person will also be responsible for leading, providing direction, resources, and guidance to ensure that all GMP quality processes are executed with the highest standards of compliance with FDA, EMA, and other international regulatory requirements, corporate objectives, and industry best practices. This role also involves ensuring that the GMP and GDP quality functions are closely aligned with the organization’s broader strategic goals, guaranteeing that quality initiatives support the company’s mission, vision, and operational objectives.

**JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Serve as the GMP quality strategic leader to assist the head of quality to further develop the quality culture at Mirum to be compliant, collaborative and phase appropriate.
* Develop and execute a global GMP quality strategy to align with corporate goals and regulatory requirements.
* Serve as the GMP quality strategic leader within the Quality group to lead the GMP QA and QC functional teams in fostering professional development and guiding staff in all aspects of GMP/GDP competence in meeting domestic and international regulatory requirements and guidelines (FDA, EMA, MHRA, NMPA, ICH, etc.).
* Lead the development and optimization of key processes, functional collaboration, transformational initiatives, and operational excellence through the GMP/GDP Quality Unit.
* Serve as the GMP quality lead in Audits and Regulatory Inspections in providing strategic leadership, interactions, responses, CAPA plans and implementation.
* Lead the GMP inspection readiness for the Company including GMP Quality improvement and maintenance.
* Host/Manage GMP PAI/PLI inspections at Mirum and support Mirum PAI/PLI related CMO inspections.
* Drive corporate values, vision, goals, and objectives through collaboration with senior leaders building cross-functional networks to influence operational capabilities.
* Serve as a GMP Quality advisor to cross-functional stakeholders within Mirum global organizations and subsidiaries.
* Promote collaboration across internal and external functional teams and stakeholders to identify, design and implement opportunities for improvement across all areas of GMP and GDP quality responsibilities.
* Establish, maintain, and ensure effectiveness of GMP and GDP quality programs and documentation to assure GxP compliance in the domestic and international regulatory environment.
* Oversee, support and perform all aspects of GMP QA and QC activities and functions for drug manufacturing to ensure product quality and supply chain integrity.
* Oversee and support all aspects of clinical and commercial product release which includes direct to market, partner and distributor.
* Serve as the Material Review Board (MRB) chair-person designee.
* Develop and execute a global recall strategy that integrates domestic and international recalls.
* Serve as the Recall Coordinator in the recall committee and support the recall/mock recall process.
* Collaborate with Commercial Organization on launch strategies, NPP/EAP/CUP programs and provide input as a Quality SME.
* Review and approval of GMP, GDP, Partner and Distributor Quality/Technical Agreements.
* Oversee the review and approval of APQR generation in a timely fashion.
* Assess the outcome of GMP audits at CMOs, CTLs, Partners, etc. for a holistic view and to partner with the Technical Operations team in driving improvements.
* Provide strategic and managerial leadership related to company objectives & initiatives and changing regulatory requirements to build, manage, and mentor high-performance QA and QC teams in a global environment.
* Oversee product launch, manufacturing, and distribution quality processes.
* Lead a culture of quality excellence, compliance, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* Ensure global GMP Quality Team meets stakeholder needs, focusing on efficiency, quality, budget management, and corporate growth.
* Serve as Quality Head designee for other GXP areas beyond GMP and GDP as required.
* Requires 15% domestic and international travel, at minimum.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education /Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in biochemistry, chemistry, biology, or other science related field (Advanced degree preferred).
* 15+ years of progressive Quality Assurance experience in pharmaceutical and/or Biotech industries, with at least 10+ years in quality leadership role and/or people management including direct & indirect reports.
* Demonstrates extensive knowledge of cGMP manufacturing and Quality Management in compliance with FDA (CBER and/or CDER) and EMA requirements for global-regulated products.
* Demonstrates extensive knowledge of the development and commercialization of medical device in compliance with FDA 21CFR820, ISO13485 and EMA MDR regulations
* Comprehensive knowledge of GMP, GDP, ISO, ICH, and global regulatory requirements.
* Product lifecycle including Late-stage drug development, Regulatory (NDA, MAA, BLA, etc) submission and commercial manufacturing experience.
* Experience with hosting and preparing for inspection readiness and an ability to provide recommendations for its continuous improvement.
* Must be able to work cross functionally as a strong collaborator with ability to partner with internal and external stakeholders across multiple global regions.
* Experience with managing Product Quality Complaints and Pharmacovigilance Quality is a plus
* Experience in rare disease and/or biologics, a plus.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

* Extensive hands-on experience in product lifecycle management including late-phase innovative drug development, medical device, combination product and global commercial launch with global CMC regulatory filings (IND/IMPD/CTA/NDA/BLA/MAA, etc.) in a multinational pharmaceutical organization.
* Demonstrate project and cross-functional team leadership, as well as people management skills across different cultures.
* Thorough understanding and working experience in innovative drug development and manufacturing of drugs and biologics concerning GMP operations, quality systems, ICH guidelines, FDA, EMA, and associated international regulatory requirements.
* Extensive working experience with management and oversight of the analytical activities at CDMOs or CTLs with quality mind-set and leadership.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with strategic and sound technically driven decision-making ability.
* Highly effective and strong ability to influence and lead cross-functional teams.
* Strong sense of ethics and honesty.
* Ability to communicate with all levels of management and peers within the organization.
* Effective written and verbal communication skills and interpersonal skills.

The salary range for this position is $320,000 to $340,000 USD. Compensation will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to; skill set, years of experience, and the employee’s geographic location. Please note that the required compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include bonus, equity, or benefits unless otherwise provided.

existing_roles.description:
At CompoSecure, we are redefining the future of payment card technology. As a global leader in premium metal payment cards and fintech solutions, we combine innovation with craftsmanship to deliver exceptional products for the world's leading financial institutions.
  
  
We're looking for talented individuals who share our passion for excellence and innovation.
  
  
**Position Overview**
This role provides senior leadership and ownership of the functions that safeguard product integrity and the operating environment: Quality, Compliance (Quality Control, Quality Assurance, Safety and regulatory conformance), Security, and Facilities. The position is accountable for ensuring that products consistently meet quality specifications, that operations remain fully compliant with regulatory and safety standards, that the site and its products are secure, and that facilities are maintained to support a reliable 24/7 manufacturing environment. The role establishes clear metrics and ownership across these areas and reports performance to senior leadership.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Quality: Establish and maintain quality control protocols for raw materials, components, and finished products. Design inspection and testing processes and provide guidance on maintaining consistent quality from the beginning of production through final release. Lead Quality Assurance and Quality Control teams, monitor quality metrics, and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to eliminate root causes of defects. Ensure conformance to customer, product, and industry specifications.
* Compliance: Ensure full compliance of operations with ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and applicable safety standards in accordance with New Jersey law. Own audits, certifications, and documentation, and serve as the primary liaison with regulatory bodies, auditors, and customers on compliance matters. Identify potential risks and pitfalls (e.g., equipment failures or other disruptions) and develop strategies to mitigate these issues through process improvement, alternative suppliers of materials, or altered equipment.
* Security: Oversee physical and product security programs consistent with the company's trust and authentication mission. Establish and enforce protocols to protect raw materials, work-in-process, finished goods, and sensitive assets throughout the facility and supply chain. Ensure operations meet payment-industry and customer security requirements, and manage security personnel and access controls across all shifts.
* Accountability: Own the key performance indicators and reporting for quality, compliance, security, and facilities. Establish clear ownership, metrics, and dashboards, report performance to senior management, and foster a culture of accountability across the organization. Manage a team of approximately 35 people across 7 shifts supporting QA, Safety & Security.
* Facilities: Oversee facility operations, maintenance, and environmental health and safety of the buildings, grounds, and utilities. Ensure facilities are maintained to support a reliable 24/7 manufacturing environment, manage facility vendors and contractors, and lead facility-related capital projects, space planning, and safe-workplace initiatives.

**Skills & Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Quality, Operations Management, or a related field.
* A minimum of 10–15 years (or more) of relevant experience in quality, compliance, and/or operations leadership in a high-volume manufacturing environment (Pharmaceutical, Semiconductor, Automotive, or secure/payment products) , with at least 5-10 years experience in managing teams across multiple shift in a 24/7 environment :
* Deep knowledge of quality management systems (ISO 9001, IATF 16949 for automotive, AS9100 for aerospace, etc.)
* Six Sigma / Lean methodologies (typically Black Belt or Master Black Belt level)
* Root cause analysis and CAPA (corrective and preventive action) processes
* Statistical process control (SPC) and data-driven decision making
* Supplier quality management and audit experience
* Very strong analytical skill set, including familiarity with quality and reliability tools (e.g., FMEA, SPC, Kaizen).
* Regulatory fluency:
* OSHA, EPA, ISO 14001 (environmental), ISO 45001 (occupational health & safety)
* Industrial hygiene and risk assessment methodologies
* Environmental compliance (emissions, waste management, hazmat handling)
* Process safety management
* Incident investigation and workers' compensation/claims oversight
* Demonstrated experience working with cross-functional teams required.
* Demonstrated experience in third party audits ( ISO , PCI, ....)
* Occasional travel to suppliers and partners.

**Preferred Skills And Qualifications**

* Quality certifications such as Black belt Six Sigma
* GHG Management
* Familiarity with ERP tools
* Experience in a secure payment, or otherwise highly regulated manufacturing environment.

**About CompoSecure**
CompoSecure, a GPGI business (NYSE: GPGI), is the leading manufacturer of Premium Metal Payment Cards and also offers best-in-class Authentication and Digital Asset solutions. The Company's offerings combine elegance, simplicity, and security to deliver exceptional experiences and peace of mind, enabling trust for millions of people around the globe. For more information, please visit
**www.CompoSecure.com**
and
**www.GetArculus.com**
.
  
  
We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance, including medical, prescription, dental, and vision coverage; FSA/HSA options; company-paid life and disability insurance; 401(k) with company match; paid time off (PTO) and holidays; annual bonus opportunities; an employee assistance program (EAP); and opportunities for career growth and advancement.
  
  
*Additional details will be provided during the hiring process.*
CompoSecure is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. We are also an equal opportunity employer of individuals with disabilities and protected veterans.
  
  
**Please note:**
CompoSecure does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies or third-party recruiters. Any unsolicited resumes sent to CompoSecure, including to our employees, will become the property of CompoSecure and may be used without any obligation to pay referral or placement fees. Any agency or recruiter seeking to work with CompoSecure's Talent Acquisition Team should contact our team directly by sending an email to
**recruiting@composecure.com**
.
  
  
CompoSecure offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and the opportunity to work alongside a team of dedicated professionals who are shaping the future of financial technology.

**Incentive Compensation**
Offers will be negotiated based on each candidate's qualifications.
  
  
This role may be eligible to participate in our annual or quarterly incentive plan. Incentives are earned based on employee performance against defined metrics and company goals.

Full-time employees are eligible for our comprehensive benefits program which includes Group Healthcare, Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Account, Group Term Life Insurance, and 401(k) retirement plan. **Vice President, Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. In this role, you will lead the global product distribution quality organization and processes, holding quality management accountability for all captive and outsourced distribution centres across every entity worldwide.

This is a genuine turnaround and organizational design mandate, rather than a caretaker or step-up role. You will step in to stabilize day-to-day operations, manage significant FDA and global regulatory scrutiny, and reshape the commercial quality infrastructure into a world-class function. For a seasoned executive who enjoys building progressive systems at scale, there is a clear path to expanded enterprise responsibility within 6 to 20 months.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Global Distribution Governance:**
  Own quality management systems/compliance performance across captive/3PL distribution centres globally - alongside full P&L, budget, and headcount accountability for the function.
* **Turnaround & Future-State Design:**
  Audit current teams, workflows, and systems to close compliance gaps, restructuring the global commercial quality organization into a streamlined, best-in-class model.
* **FDA & Global Regulatory Execution:**
  Act as the single accountable global executive for all distribution-related regulatory inspections, audit responses, and direct agency communications, including intensive FDA engagement.
* **Quality Systems & Digital Traceability:**
  Direct the IT partnership to optimize warehouse management systems (WMS), end-to-end product traceability, inventory controls, and nonconforming product containment.
* **Enterprise Leadership:**
  Serve as the global subject matter expert for distribution quality and contribute to enterprise-wide quality strategy as a senior member of the Global Corporate Quality leadership team.

**Candidate Profile**

* **Sitting or Recent Med-Tech VP:**
  Minimum 10 years of global organizational leadership at the Vice President level within medical devices, capital equipment, or adjacent life sciences—ready to deliver impact from day one.
* **Post-Manufacturing & 3PL Mastery:**
  Deep operational expertise in commercial, supply chain, and global distribution quality across multi-site networks (upstream supplier quality into manufacturing is out of scope).
* **Proven Remediation Track Record:**
  Demonstrated success leading quality turnarounds, organizational redesigns, and systemic remediation under active FDA scrutiny.
* **Global Trade & Customs Compliance:**
  Hands-on command of international medical device regulations, import/export laws, embargoes, import bans, and regional market-entry barriers.
* **Academic Foundation:**
  Bachelor of Science in a medical or applied science discipline

**What Sets You Apart**

You lead from the front with high energy and a clear appetite for complex turnarounds. You combine sharp analytical rigor with executive presence, enabling you to influence across commercial, supply chain, and regulatory stakeholders while building high-performing global teams.

**Job Description**
**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.

**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.

**Preferred**

* Experience with API development and manufacturing processes
* Certification in Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma

* Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear.
* Frequently required to use hands to handle or feel objects, reach with hands and arms, and climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* Regular work in a standard office environment, with frequent entry into the production area of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility.
* Production environment may include moving mechanical parts, fumes or airborne particles, extreme heat, wet or humid conditions, low levels of toxic or caustic chemicals, and outdoor weather conditions.
* Noise level in the work environment is typically moderate.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
  
  
**About The Role**
We’re hiring a Director of Manufacturing Operations to oversee all production within our Air Dominance & Strike division, from rapidly maturing prototypes through full-rate production at scale.
  
  
In this role, you will be responsible for managing a team of highly talented managers, line supervisors, and technicians who manufacture both our current key autonomous products, Fury, Barracuda, and Roadrunner, and our emerging capabilities. This is a highly dynamic role that requires both technical and frontline people management skills. This role is at the forefront of delivering exceptional customer experiences, fostering team development, and overseeing operations at Arsenal-01 and HQ.
  
  
As a Director in the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. This role is crucial in ensuring that both manufacturing sites and operations align with the division's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, in addition to balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's manufacturing operational success.
  
  
Success in this role demands consistent achievement across hardware production, team management, manufacturing operations, and financial goals. The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with effective communication, strong time-management skills, and a passion for leading transformative change. *New York, New York, United States (Hybrid – 3 days/week in office)*
Who We Are
  
  
At Pets + People, we make tails wag and customers smile with products brought to market through strategic licensing and innovation. Our brands make everyday life fresh, fun, and user-friendly for the whole family.
  
  
Our team of over 80 dedicated employees is headquartered in New York City with both national and global support. With our background, experience, and network, we are uniquely positioned to extend the reach of any brand to a new market.
  
  
“We’ve been a pioneer in licensing since 2008, translating favorite brands into practical ‘pet’ applications. In 2014, we expanded our vision into new markets within the ‘people’ sector. Now, we are leveraging our long track record of success and applying it both to pets + people.” – Steven Shweky, Top Dog
  
  
**About The Role**
Learn more about our capabilities at www.petspeople.com
  
  
We are seeking a dynamic and forward-thinking Director of Production to lead and evolve our global production organization within a fast-paced Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) environment. This role is critical in driving operational excellence across both domestic and international production, while also reimagining how production can be more innovative, automated, and scalable as the business grows.
  
  
The ideal candidate is a hands-on leader who thrives in complexity, can manage a large SKU portfolio across multiple markets, builds strong global vendor partnerships, and inspires teams through coaching and mentorship. This person will lead on behalf of the department head when needed and serve as a strategic thought partner across the organization. We are open to candidates from a variety of industries, provided they bring transferable production leadership experience and a passion for continuous improvement.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  
Global Production Leadership & Strategy
  
  

* Lead end-to-end domestic and international production operations, with ownership of the full purchase order (PO) lifecycle from placement through manufacturing, delivery, and payment.
* Develop and execute production strategies that support growth, scalability, and on-time delivery across multiple regions and manufacturing partners.
* Act as a senior leader within the organization, representing the production function and driving alignment across cross-functional teams.
* Proactively manage capacity, timing, and execution risk across a high-volume, high-SKU environment.

Innovation & Automation
  
  

* Identify and implement process improvements, automation, and system enhancements to improve speed, visibility, and decision-making.
* Reduce manual work and streamline production workflows across teams and departments.
* Champion data-driven production management through clear metrics, dashboards, and reporting.

Vendor & External Partner Management
  
  

* Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with domestic and international manufacturing partners.
* Establish and manage supplier performance metrics, including on-time delivery, lead time reliability, and execution accuracy.
* Drive continuous improvement and cost optimization across the production lifecycle.
* Maintain disciplined execution and strong supplier performance management.
* Act as the primary escalation point for vendor execution, capacity, and delivery risks.

People Leadership & Development
  
  

* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing production team, fostering a culture of accountability, growth, and engagement.
* Build clear organizational structure, roles, and communication rhythms to support scale.
* Develop future leaders through coaching, feedback, and development planning.

Operational Excellence & Scale
  
  

* Strengthen operational rigor through standardized workflows and clear cross-functional handoffs.
* Identify and proactively address risks related to capacity, cost, supply continuity, and execution across domestic and international production.
* Ensure production operations are scalable to support rapid growth and evolving business needs.

What You'll Bring
  
  

* 10+ years of progressive experience in production, manufacturing, or operations leadership; CPG experience strongly preferred, but industry background is flexible.
* Proven success managing both domestic and international production operations.
* Experience managing and developing teams of 5–10; a hands-on people leader with a passion for coaching, mentoring, and team development within a lean, high-output team structure.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex production environments with large SKU counts.
* Track record of driving process improvement, innovation, and automation.
* Strong global vendor management and negotiation experience.
* Bilingual in Chinese and English preferred.
* Strategic thinker with the ability to execute at a detailed, operational level.
* Comfortable operating in an evolving environment.
* Strong proficiency in Excel; tech-savvy and resourceful, with a demonstrated ability to quickly adopt new systems, tools, and platforms as the business scales.

Hybrid Work
  
  
We're a hybrid office culture, in office 3 days per week with flexibility to work from home the rest. We value the connection and collaboration that in-person work brings, while giving our team room to work in the way that's most effective for them.
  
  
**Compensation**
The salary range for this role is $150,000 – $165,000 per year, depending on experience, skills, and location.
  
  
Hybrid Work
  
  
We're a hybrid office culture, in office 3 days a week with flexibility to work from home the rest. We value the connection and collaboration that in-person work brings, while giving our team room to work in the way that's most effective for them.

* Medical, Dental & Vision insurance
* HSA/FSA options

* Generous vacation, personal, and wellness days that grow with tenure

* Pet-friendly office
* Hybrid flexible schedule, with additional Work-From-Anywhere days throughout the year

All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, age, religion, disability, citizenship status, national origin, pregnancy, veteran status, and any other factor protected by applicable law.

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. **Job Duties**
The Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations is a senior operations leader responsible for translating site strategy into strong operational execution. Responsibilities are aligned to three core competency areas:
  
  
**Operational & Strategic Execution**

* Own day‑to‑day production quality performance, applying a zero‑defect mindset using traditional quality methodologies (8D, 5‑Why, SPC) and AI‑assisted defect detection, yield analysis, and trend identification.

Occasional night or weekend hours are required to support operational needs.
