**Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality**

**Location:** Lakewood, Ohio  
**Company:** Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company  
**Employment Type:** Full Time  
**Reports To:** President

**About Ferry Cap**

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is a long-established American manufacturer of engineered fasteners and specialty metal components serving demanding industrial and power generation applications. As we invest in our people, equipment, and operating systems, we are seeking a senior quality leader who can help strengthen our processes and build a companywide culture of quality.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will lead Ferry Cap’s quality organization and serve as a key member of the company’s leadership team.

This is a hands on leadership position for someone with strong experience in metallurgy, metal transformation, manufacturing processes, and heat treatment. The successful candidate will work closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, supply chain, and customers to improve process control, solve technical problems, and ensure consistent product quality.

The right leader will view quality as an operating partnership, not simply an inspection function. This individual must be comfortable working on the production floor, engaging directly with employees, and helping build quality into every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all quality assurance, quality control, laboratory, inspection, and quality systems activities.
* Partner directly with operations to establish a culture in which safety, delivery, quality, and cost are shared responsibilities.
* Provide technical leadership related to metallurgy, raw materials, metal forming, metal transformation, machining, threading, and heat treatment.
* Oversee metallurgical testing and analysis, including hardness, microstructure, case depth, decarburization, mechanical properties, material certification, and failure analysis.
* Evaluate and improve heat treatment processes, including furnace controls, quenching, tempering, process consistency, and product conformance.
* Strengthen incoming, in process, and final inspection systems to ensure product requirements are consistently achieved.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action activities involving internal defects, customer complaints, supplier issues, and process failures.
* Use structured problem solving methods such as 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and MSA.
* Maintain and continuously improve the company’s quality management system, documentation, procedures, work instructions, and audit processes.
* Ensure compliance with customer requirements, industry standards, specifications, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Lead customer audits, supplier audits, internal audits, and customer quality reviews.
* Build strong working relationships with customer quality and engineering teams.
* Develop meaningful quality metrics, including first pass yield, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, corrective action effectiveness, and supplier performance.
* Improve material traceability and process control throughout the manufacturing operation.
* Lead supplier quality development and ensure purchased materials and outside processes meet Ferry Cap requirements.
* Develop, coach, and hold accountable the quality team while strengthening quality knowledge throughout the organization.
* Support new product introduction, process changes, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish clear containment, escalation, and corrective action processes when quality concerns arise.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant quality leadership experience in a metal manufacturing environment.
* Strong practical knowledge of metallurgy, material properties, metal transformation, and heat treatment.
* Experience with manufacturing processes such as cold forming, forging, machining, threading, rolling, or similar metalworking operations.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose metallurgical and manufacturing process failures.
* Experience leading quality systems, customer audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong working knowledge of dimensional inspection, mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, calibration, and measurement systems.
* Experience using quality tools such as PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis.
* Proven ability to work collaboratively with operations and engineering teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem solving skills.
* Willingness to spend significant time on the manufacturing floor and become personally involved in resolving issues.
* Bachelor’s degree in metallurgy, materials science, engineering, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant manufacturing experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including at least five years in a leadership role.
* Experience with engineered fasteners, high strength components, critical industrial products, or power generation applications.
* Experience with ISO based quality management systems and customer specific quality requirements.
* Experience working with commercial heat treat suppliers and internal heat treatment operations.
* ASQ certification, Six Sigma certification, or formal Lean manufacturing training.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.

**Leadership Profile**

The successful candidate will be:

* Hands on and comfortable working directly with production employees.
* Collaborative and capable of building trust across departments.
* Technically strong, practical, and decisive.
* Focused on preventing defects instead of relying on inspection to find them.
* Comfortable challenging existing practices while respecting Ferry Cap’s people and history.
* Able to balance customer requirements with operational realities.
* Committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and developing others.

**Why Join Ferry Cap**

This position offers the opportunity to play a major role in the continued transformation and growth of a historic American manufacturing company. The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will have direct access to company leadership, meaningful influence over operations, and the opportunity to build a quality culture that supports Ferry Cap’s customers, employees, and long term success.

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

This role represents a critical executive leadership opportunity for a dynamic Director of Operations – Chillers to join the Global Operations team. existing_roles.title: Director, Strategy & Operations
existing_roles.description:
**The Problem**

Severe mental illness affects over 15 million adults in the United States. Schizophrenia. Schizoaffective disorder. Bipolar I. Treatment-resistant depression. These are the conditions the rest of healthcare has systematically failed to build for.

What makes this problem different from most of healthcare is that the tools to solve it do not exist. The clinical protocols, the measurement science, the precision medicine, the technology to deliver coordinated longitudinal outpatient care for this population. None of it has been built. This is a frontier problem, and it requires frontier science and care delivery to solve.

We are developing all of it. The care, the science, the technology.

**Who We Are**

Amae Health is a Series B, venture-backed Public Benefit Corporation delivering specialty outpatient care for people with severe mental illness through high-acuity, in-person clinics nationwide.

Our integrated model brings psychiatry, therapy, primary care, dietitians, and community support together under one roof. Leading health systems—including **New York-Presbyterian, Cedars-Sinai, Mass General Brigham, Novant Health, and CommonSpirit**—collaborate with us to expand this level of care.

Alongside care delivery, we are building the science and technology the field has long lacked—proprietary clinical protocols, novel measurement, and an AI-driven data platform designed for severe mental illness.

The impact: fewer hospitalizations, greater stability, and more people living meaningful lives in their communities.

**The Team**

We are clinicians, operators, technologists, and scientists who chose Amae because the problem is hard and the stakes are real. We are not interested in incremental improvements to a broken system—we are redefining it.

Every function—finance, product, people, growth, technology—exists to serve one goal: better outcomes for the people we care for.

**The Role**

Amae Health is looking for a **Director of Strategy & Operations** to help scale a fundamentally new model of care for individuals with severe mental illness. This is a high-impact, hands-on leadership role spanning **market expansion, growth, and operational excellence**.

You'll work closely with executive, clinical, and operational leaders to **launch new markets, accelerate growth in existing ones, and build the systems that enable Amae to scale**. From developing go-to-market strategies to solving complex operational challenges, you'll turn ambitious goals into measurable results.

We're looking for a **strategic thinker who loves to execute** — someone who can see the big picture, dive into the details, and build what doesn't yet exist.

  

**What You'll Own**

* **Drive market expansion and new launches.** Lead go-to-market strategy and execution for new clinics, services, and markets — from identifying opportunities and developing launch plans to ensuring successful rollout and early performance.
* **Own high-impact growth and operational initiatives.** Identify and lead the highest-leverage opportunities to accelerate growth, improve referral conversion, strengthen care delivery, and increase operational efficiency.
* **Build the playbook for scale.** Design the operating models, processes, and performance management systems that allow Amae to grow rapidly without compromising quality or consistency of care.
* **Turn complex problems into measurable results.** Use data, frontline insights, and structured problem-solving to uncover bottlenecks, develop solutions, and drive improvements from hypothesis through implementation.
* **Lead across functions to make things happen.** Partner with clinical, operations, growth, and product leaders to translate strategic priorities into coordinated execution, navigating ambiguity and driving accountability along the way.
* **Shape how Amae operates as we grow.** Work closely with senior leadership to tackle emerging business challenges, test new approaches, and turn what works into repeatable systems across our care delivery network.

**What You'll Bring**

* **7+ years of experience** in strategy, operations, growth, or general management, ideally in a high-growth startup, consulting firm, or healthcare organization.
* **A track record of turning strategy into results.** You've owned complex, high-impact initiatives from identifying the opportunity to driving execution and delivering measurable outcomes.
* **A builder's mindset.** You thrive in ambiguity, move quickly, and are energized by creating structure, processes, and solutions where no playbook exists.
* **Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.** You can break down ambiguous problems, use data to inform decisions, and balance strategic thinking with practical execution.
* **Commercial instincts.** You're excited to drive growth, expand into new markets, build partnerships, and identify opportunities to improve business performance.
* **The ability to lead through influence.** You're collaborative, high-EQ, and effective at aligning diverse stakeholders — from frontline clinical teams to executive leadership — without relying on formal authority.
* **A genuine connection to our mission.** Healthcare experience is a plus, not a prerequisite. You're motivated by the opportunity to transform care for individuals with severe mental illness.
* **Based in the SF Bay Area**, with the ability to work in person five days a week at our Cow Hollow office.

**What We're Building**

Most healthcare companies ask you to optimize an existing system. We're building one that has never existed.

* A national care model designed for the highest-acuity patients in behavioral health.
* Precision medicine for severe mental illness, using multimodal clinical, behavioral, and social data to personalize treatment.
* A clinical operating system that integrates longitudinal data, real-time patient signals, and purpose-built tools into a single decision layer.
* New science and measurement frameworks to define what real outcomes look like in SMI—stability, functional improvement, and hospitalizations avoided.
* A health-system partnership model proving coordinated SMI care can work at scale.

If you want to maintain the status quo, this isn't the place. If you want to build what doesn't exist yet—and change how an entire population receives care—keep reading.

**What We Value**

**We center care in all we do.** Empathy is not a brand value. It's how we make clinical decisions, build products, and treat each other.

**We challenge convention.** The existing system is the problem. We question it, we test alternatives, and we move with urgency when something works.

**We take the work seriously, not ourselves.** High standards and humanity are not in tension. We hold a hard bar for quality while leaving room for humor and levity.

**Your job isn't done until the job is done.** We close gaps, we follow through, and we don't hide behind titles or org charts.

**We win together and fail together.** We own outcomes as a team. We learn fast. We don't do blame.

**We hustle with humility.** Speed matters. So does integrity. We assume best intent and stay grounded in the mission.

**Compensation & Benefits**

Amae Health is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. **Base salary range for this role is $165,000–$200,000 per year**, adjusted to market cost; the compensation package may include equity. Total compensation includes comprehensive medical/dental/vision, unlimited PTO, parental leave, and programs built around employee well-being. We'll share specifics during the interview process.

*Amae Health is building the care platform, the precision medicine, and the frontier science that severe mental illness has never had. If you want to be part of creating something this hard and this important, something that has never been done, we'd like to talk.*

Imagine starting your day on the production floor—checking safety, huddling with supervisors, scanning your ERP dashboard, and walking a focused gemba to spot the next opportunity. We equip learners and employers with hands-on training systems, interactive eLearning, simulators, curriculum, and certification resources that turn complex technology into practical skill. existing_roles.description:
Your Contribution
=================

The Head of Plant Production Engineering is responsible for leading all Production Engineering activities associated with customer projects, product acquisitions, new product launches, industrialization, and production readiness within the plant. This position serves as the plant's primary owner for Production Engineering processes, ensuring successful execution of the Product Development Process (PDP) from acquisition through Start of Production (SOP) and ramp-up. The role provides leadership to Production Engineers, drives standardization and deployment of manufacturing concepts, ensures manufacturability of product designs, manages capital investments, and represents Operations within project core teams. The Plant Head of Production Engineering ensures project launches meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and operational performance objectives.

* Lead, develop, coach, & manage the plant Production Engineering organization.
* Build organizational capability to support current and future product launches.
* Own industrialization activities for all customer projects within the plant. Ensure successful execution of product launches from acquisition and business transfer through SOP and stabilization.
* Lead development of manufacturing concepts, production processes, line layouts, and assembly strategies.
* Ensure product designs are manufacturable and meet operational standards.
* Coordinate launch readiness across Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling Engineering, Quality, Logistics, Purchasing, and Operations Support acquisition reviews and participate in PAC, PRC, and pre-development activities.
* Ensure implementation of Design-for-Manufacturing principles throughout project development. Ensure compliance with MAHLE PDP milestones, gates, deliverables, and timing requirements. Oversee completion of all Production Engineering deliverables throughout all quality gates.
* Monitor project status, risks, cost performance, capacity requirements, and launch readiness. Lead escalation activities when project risks threaten timing, quality, or cost objectives. Review project dashboards and launch metrics with plant leadership and program teams.
* Approve and govern: Manufacturing concepts, Process flows, Plant layouts, Assembly concepts, Material flow strategies, Value stream integration.
* Ensure application of Lean Manufacturing and Manufacturing Optimization Process (MOP) methodologies in alignment with Operations Excellence Manager.
* Drive takt-time analysis, line balancing, ergonomic studies, and capacity planning. Validate cycle times using MTM or equivalent engineering methods. Ensure implementation of standardized manufacturing processes across the region.
* Ensure development, completion, and approval of Process FMEA (P-FMEA), Control Plans, Special Characteristics, Process Capability Studies, Validation Plans. Support flawless launch activities and manufacturing risk reduction. Lead readiness reviews for installation checks, internal process approval, internal run at rate, customer run at rate, PPAP readiness. Ensure production systems consistently achieve quality and operational KPI’s.
* Lead capital expenditure planning and approval activities. Validate business cases and investment requirements. Ensure optimal utilization of existing equipment before requesting new capital. Support supplier selection through PDC and SDC processes. Approve manufacturing equipment specifications. Participate in procurement and acceptance of production equipment, tooling, fixtures, and test systems.
* Chair Production Engineering project meetings, and lead the plant Production Engineering Extended Team, ensuring effective communication between Project Core Teams and Plant Extended Teams.

Your Experience & Qualifications

* Bachelor’s Degree required, B.S. in Engineering, or related technical discipline required. Master’s Degree preferred.
* 8+ years’ experience in manufacturing, launch, industrialization, or production engineering.
* 5+ years’ progressive leadership responsibility regarding engineering or manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated success in leading complex product launches and PDP projects.
* Experience in an automotive manufacturing facility required; high volume, medium to large campus experience preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge in IATF16949, ISO14001 and 45001 Audits and processes.
* Excellent diagnostic abilities / root cause analysis required; Lean Six Sigma and Black Belt certification strongly preferred.

We will provide a collaborative environment working on exciting assignments, along with ongoing personal & career development opportunities. At CompoSecure, we are redefining the future of payment card technology. As a global leader in premium metal payment cards and fintech solutions, we combine innovation with craftsmanship to deliver exceptional products for the world's leading financial institutions.
  
  
We're looking for talented individuals who share our passion for excellence and innovation.
  
  
**Position Overview**
This role provides senior leadership and ownership of the functions that safeguard product integrity and the operating environment: Quality, Compliance (Quality Control, Quality Assurance, Safety and regulatory conformance), Security, and Facilities. The position is accountable for ensuring that products consistently meet quality specifications, that operations remain fully compliant with regulatory and safety standards, that the site and its products are secure, and that facilities are maintained to support a reliable 24/7 manufacturing environment. The role establishes clear metrics and ownership across these areas and reports performance to senior leadership.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Quality: Establish and maintain quality control protocols for raw materials, components, and finished products. Design inspection and testing processes and provide guidance on maintaining consistent quality from the beginning of production through final release. Lead Quality Assurance and Quality Control teams, monitor quality metrics, and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to eliminate root causes of defects. Ensure conformance to customer, product, and industry specifications.
* Compliance: Ensure full compliance of operations with ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and applicable safety standards in accordance with New Jersey law. Own audits, certifications, and documentation, and serve as the primary liaison with regulatory bodies, auditors, and customers on compliance matters. Identify potential risks and pitfalls (e.g., equipment failures or other disruptions) and develop strategies to mitigate these issues through process improvement, alternative suppliers of materials, or altered equipment.
* Security: Oversee physical and product security programs consistent with the company's trust and authentication mission. Establish and enforce protocols to protect raw materials, work-in-process, finished goods, and sensitive assets throughout the facility and supply chain. Ensure operations meet payment-industry and customer security requirements, and manage security personnel and access controls across all shifts.
* Accountability: Own the key performance indicators and reporting for quality, compliance, security, and facilities. Establish clear ownership, metrics, and dashboards, report performance to senior management, and foster a culture of accountability across the organization. Manage a team of approximately 35 people across 7 shifts supporting QA, Safety & Security.
* Facilities: Oversee facility operations, maintenance, and environmental health and safety of the buildings, grounds, and utilities. Ensure facilities are maintained to support a reliable 24/7 manufacturing environment, manage facility vendors and contractors, and lead facility-related capital projects, space planning, and safe-workplace initiatives.

**Skills & Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Quality, Operations Management, or a related field.
* A minimum of 10–15 years (or more) of relevant experience in quality, compliance, and/or operations leadership in a high-volume manufacturing environment (Pharmaceutical, Semiconductor, Automotive, or secure/payment products) , with at least 5-10 years experience in managing teams across multiple shift in a 24/7 environment :
* Deep knowledge of quality management systems (ISO 9001, IATF 16949 for automotive, AS9100 for aerospace, etc.)
* Six Sigma / Lean methodologies (typically Black Belt or Master Black Belt level)
* Root cause analysis and CAPA (corrective and preventive action) processes
* Statistical process control (SPC) and data-driven decision making
* Supplier quality management and audit experience
* Very strong analytical skill set, including familiarity with quality and reliability tools (e.g., FMEA, SPC, Kaizen).
* Regulatory fluency:
* OSHA, EPA, ISO 14001 (environmental), ISO 45001 (occupational health & safety)
* Industrial hygiene and risk assessment methodologies
* Environmental compliance (emissions, waste management, hazmat handling)
* Process safety management
* Incident investigation and workers' compensation/claims oversight
* Demonstrated experience working with cross-functional teams required.
* Demonstrated experience in third party audits ( ISO , PCI, ....)
* Occasional travel to suppliers and partners.

**Preferred Skills And Qualifications**

* Quality certifications such as Black belt Six Sigma
* GHG Management
* Familiarity with ERP tools
* Experience in a secure payment, or otherwise highly regulated manufacturing environment.

**About CompoSecure**
CompoSecure, a GPGI business (NYSE: GPGI), is the leading manufacturer of Premium Metal Payment Cards and also offers best-in-class Authentication and Digital Asset solutions. The Company's offerings combine elegance, simplicity, and security to deliver exceptional experiences and peace of mind, enabling trust for millions of people around the globe. For more information, please visit
**www.CompoSecure.com**
and
**www.GetArculus.com**
.

**Vice President, Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. In this role, you will lead the global product distribution quality organization and processes, holding quality management accountability for all captive and outsourced distribution centres across every entity worldwide.

This is a genuine turnaround and organizational design mandate, rather than a caretaker or step-up role. You will step in to stabilize day-to-day operations, manage significant FDA and global regulatory scrutiny, and reshape the commercial quality infrastructure into a world-class function. For a seasoned executive who enjoys building progressive systems at scale, there is a clear path to expanded enterprise responsibility within 6 to 20 months.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Global Distribution Governance:**
  Own quality management systems/compliance performance across captive/3PL distribution centres globally - alongside full P&L, budget, and headcount accountability for the function.
* **Turnaround & Future-State Design:**
  Audit current teams, workflows, and systems to close compliance gaps, restructuring the global commercial quality organization into a streamlined, best-in-class model.
* **FDA & Global Regulatory Execution:**
  Act as the single accountable global executive for all distribution-related regulatory inspections, audit responses, and direct agency communications, including intensive FDA engagement.
* **Quality Systems & Digital Traceability:**
  Direct the IT partnership to optimize warehouse management systems (WMS), end-to-end product traceability, inventory controls, and nonconforming product containment.
* **Enterprise Leadership:**
  Serve as the global subject matter expert for distribution quality and contribute to enterprise-wide quality strategy as a senior member of the Global Corporate Quality leadership team.

**Candidate Profile**

* **Sitting or Recent Med-Tech VP:**
  Minimum 10 years of global organizational leadership at the Vice President level within medical devices, capital equipment, or adjacent life sciences—ready to deliver impact from day one.
* **Post-Manufacturing & 3PL Mastery:**
  Deep operational expertise in commercial, supply chain, and global distribution quality across multi-site networks (upstream supplier quality into manufacturing is out of scope).
* **Proven Remediation Track Record:**
  Demonstrated success leading quality turnarounds, organizational redesigns, and systemic remediation under active FDA scrutiny.
* **Global Trade & Customs Compliance:**
  Hands-on command of international medical device regulations, import/export laws, embargoes, import bans, and regional market-entry barriers.
* **Academic Foundation:**
  Bachelor of Science in a medical or applied science discipline

**What Sets You Apart**

You lead from the front with high energy and a clear appetite for complex turnarounds. You combine sharp analytical rigor with executive presence, enabling you to influence across commercial, supply chain, and regulatory stakeholders while building high-performing global teams.

**Job Description**
**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.
  
  
**Essential Responsibilities**
**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

**Good Manufacturing & Documentation Practices**
Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.
  
  

* Perform all documentation in compliance with ALCOA++ principles and site SOPs.
* Adhere to applicable cGMP documents including SOPs, batch records, protocols, change controls, and controlled forms.
* Keep all required cGMP training current and escalate quality concerns along with proposed solutions to the Quality department.

**Qualifications**
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
* Minimum 5–10 years of mid to senior management experience in a manufacturing or process environment
* Demonstrated understanding of the responsibilities and functions of key departments within a pharmaceutical or industrial manufacturing facility
* Strong knowledge of cGMP compliance, technical operations, and quality systems within a manufacturing environment
* Proven ability to identify, develop, and inspire leaders at multiple levels of the organization
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to present strategy and performance clearly to site and functional leadership

**Preferred**

* Experience with API development and manufacturing processes
* Certification in Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma

**Physical Requirements**
The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear.
* Frequently required to use hands to handle or feel objects, reach with hands and arms, and climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**
The work environment characteristics described below are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regular work in a standard office environment, with frequent entry into the production area of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
  
  
**About The Role**
We’re hiring a Director of Manufacturing Operations to oversee all production within our Air Dominance & Strike division, from rapidly maturing prototypes through full-rate production at scale.
  
  
In this role, you will be responsible for managing a team of highly talented managers, line supervisors, and technicians who manufacture both our current key autonomous products, Fury, Barracuda, and Roadrunner, and our emerging capabilities. This is a highly dynamic role that requires both technical and frontline people management skills. This role is at the forefront of delivering exceptional customer experiences, fostering team development, and overseeing operations at Arsenal-01 and HQ.
  
  
As a Director in the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. This role is crucial in ensuring that both manufacturing sites and operations align with the division's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, in addition to balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's manufacturing operational success.
  
  
Success in this role demands consistent achievement across hardware production, team management, manufacturing operations, and financial goals. The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with effective communication, strong time-management skills, and a passion for leading transformative change. The ideal candidate should be energetic, highly organized, and deeply committed to scaling innovative products. While individual contributions are valued, teamwork is crucial for achieving the highest level of success while maintaining our Anduril culture above all.
  
  
*Please note: This role will be based at Arsenal-01 in Columbus, OH. A successful candidate will be expected to work out of Columbus, OH. Based on eligibility, relocation assistance may be available. There will likely be 25% - 50% travel required for the role.*
**What You'll Do**

* First and foremost, deliver outcomes for the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization
* Create a clear vision for Manufacturing Operations

+ You are a key leader in supporting and strengthening the vision of AD&S Production
+ Manage the portfolio of projects necessary to achieve your vision for Manufacturing Operations

* Collaborate successfully with leaders across our production organization

+ Leaders include Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Planning, Quality, and Supply Chain

* Deliver quality products, on-time and at cost

+ Own attainment for both current and emerging programs

* Own the culture on the floor

+ Be a stakeholder in all programs, policies, etc. that affect life on the floor
+ Maximize for what’s right both for Anduril’s future and maintaining a strong team culture
+ Coach, mentor and support Manufacturing Operations Managers and Production Supervisors
+ Create and maintain a high bar for excellence

* Clearly communicate up and out

+ Provide consistent and high-quality briefs both up, to Anduril Senior Leadership, and out, to AD&S Customers

* In summary, show up every day with a high level of urgency, ownership, and enthusiasm to get the job done

**Required Qualifications**

* 6+ years experience managing manufacturing and production operations
* 3+ years in a supervisor or production operations management role at the Director level or above
* 3+ years of experience as a manager of managers
* Experience managing operator / technician workforce of 100+ within direct organization
* Experience working directly and communicating with designers and engineers
* A full understanding of the product life cycle (NPI to scaled production), LEAN manufacturing principles, and change management
* Extremely reliable, organized, and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills
* You have a passion for employee development and enjoy the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran production staff
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor or Master’s degree in a technical field (engineering, business, or applied science)
* Working knowledge of AS9100 standards and OSHA laws

US Salary Range
  
  
$190,000—$252,000 USD
  
  
**Benefits**
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
  
  
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.
*For more information, Explore Our Benefits.*
**Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
  
  
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
  
  

* No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* Please always verify communications:

+ Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
+ Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

* Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

**Data Privacy**
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
  
  
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

*New York, New York, United States (Hybrid – 3 days/week in office)*
Who We Are
  
  
At Pets + People, we make tails wag and customers smile with products brought to market through strategic licensing and innovation. Our brands make everyday life fresh, fun, and user-friendly for the whole family.
  
  
Our team of over 80 dedicated employees is headquartered in New York City with both national and global support. With our background, experience, and network, we are uniquely positioned to extend the reach of any brand to a new market.
  
  
“We’ve been a pioneer in licensing since 2008, translating favorite brands into practical ‘pet’ applications. In 2014, we expanded our vision into new markets within the ‘people’ sector. Now, we are leveraging our long track record of success and applying it both to pets + people.” – Steven Shweky, Top Dog
  
  
**About The Role**
Learn more about our capabilities at www.petspeople.com
  
  
We are seeking a dynamic and forward-thinking Director of Production to lead and evolve our global production organization within a fast-paced Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) environment. This role is critical in driving operational excellence across both domestic and international production, while also reimagining how production can be more innovative, automated, and scalable as the business grows.
  
  
The ideal candidate is a hands-on leader who thrives in complexity, can manage a large SKU portfolio across multiple markets, builds strong global vendor partnerships, and inspires teams through coaching and mentorship. This person will lead on behalf of the department head when needed and serve as a strategic thought partner across the organization. We are open to candidates from a variety of industries, provided they bring transferable production leadership experience and a passion for continuous improvement.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  
Global Production Leadership & Strategy
  
  

* Lead end-to-end domestic and international production operations, with ownership of the full purchase order (PO) lifecycle from placement through manufacturing, delivery, and payment.
* Develop and execute production strategies that support growth, scalability, and on-time delivery across multiple regions and manufacturing partners.
* Act as a senior leader within the organization, representing the production function and driving alignment across cross-functional teams.
* Proactively manage capacity, timing, and execution risk across a high-volume, high-SKU environment.

Innovation & Automation
  
  

* Identify and implement process improvements, automation, and system enhancements to improve speed, visibility, and decision-making.
* Reduce manual work and streamline production workflows across teams and departments.
* Champion data-driven production management through clear metrics, dashboards, and reporting.

Vendor & External Partner Management
  
  

* Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with domestic and international manufacturing partners.
* Establish and manage supplier performance metrics, including on-time delivery, lead time reliability, and execution accuracy.
* Drive continuous improvement and cost optimization across the production lifecycle.
* Maintain disciplined execution and strong supplier performance management.
* Act as the primary escalation point for vendor execution, capacity, and delivery risks.

People Leadership & Development
  
  

* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing production team, fostering a culture of accountability, growth, and engagement.
* Build clear organizational structure, roles, and communication rhythms to support scale.
* Develop future leaders through coaching, feedback, and development planning.

Operational Excellence & Scale
  
  

* Strengthen operational rigor through standardized workflows and clear cross-functional handoffs.
* Identify and proactively address risks related to capacity, cost, supply continuity, and execution across domestic and international production.
* Ensure production operations are scalable to support rapid growth and evolving business needs.

What You'll Bring
  
  

* 10+ years of progressive experience in production, manufacturing, or operations leadership; CPG experience strongly preferred, but industry background is flexible.
* Proven success managing both domestic and international production operations.
* Experience managing and developing teams of 5–10; a hands-on people leader with a passion for coaching, mentoring, and team development within a lean, high-output team structure.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex production environments with large SKU counts.
* Track record of driving process improvement, innovation, and automation.
* Strong global vendor management and negotiation experience.
* Bilingual in Chinese and English preferred.
* Strategic thinker with the ability to execute at a detailed, operational level.
* Comfortable operating in an evolving environment.
* Strong proficiency in Excel; tech-savvy and resourceful, with a demonstrated ability to quickly adopt new systems, tools, and platforms as the business scales.

We're a hybrid office culture, in office 3 days a week with flexibility to work from home the rest. We value the connection and collaboration that in-person work brings, while giving our team room to work in the way that's most effective for them.

This position is accountable for achieving Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and Growth (SQDCG) objectives while fostering a culture of continuous improvement, associate engagement, accountability, and customer focus. The Senior Plant Manager partners with cross-functional leaders to execute site strategy, develop organizational capability, and deliver sustainable business results.
  
  
The Senior Manager, Plant Manager reports directly to the Senior Director, Operations for the Commercial Gearing Business Unit.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own full site P&L responsibility, including budgeting and demonstrating strong understanding of cost structure, margins, ROI, and operational levers.
* Lead all manufacturing operations to achieve Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and Growth (SQDCG) objectives.
* Drive operational excellence through the Regal Rexnord Business System (RBS), Lean principles, and continuous improvement.
* Evaluate and prioritize capital investments to support growth, scalability, and operational excellence.
* Build, coach, and develop a high-performing leadership team while establishing strong succession plans.
* Deliver financial commitments through productivity, inventory, cost reduction, and operational efficiency initiatives.
* Foster a culture of safety, accountability, engagement, and customer focus.
* Reinforce a strong say/do culture by delivering on commitments and holding leaders accountable for results.
* Lead timely structured problem-solving and execution to achieve sustainable operational results.
* Partner cross-functionally to support business growth, customer satisfaction, and organizational effectiveness.
* Champion Regal Rexnord Core Values while developing future leaders and organizational capability.

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, or a related technical field. Advanced degree is desired.

* Minimum 5 years of leadership experience managing salaried and hourly associates in a manufacturing environment.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and achieve sustainable improvements in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and Growth (SQDCG) performance.

* Proven ability to build, coach, and develop high-performing teams while driving accountability, engagement, and succession planning in a changing environment.
* Strong analytical, decision-making, and project management skills with a data-driven approach to problem solving.

**The Role**
Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.
  
  
Moderna is strengthening its presence in Norwood, Massachusetts, a cornerstone of our manufacturing and operational excellence. Our Norwood campus translates mRNA science into scalable impact, supporting the global delivery of our medicines. We welcome talent ready to drive innovation and make a meaningful difference for patients worldwide.
  
  
This is an opportunity to lead at the intersection of DNA Manufacturing, Cell Bank operations, Operational Excellence, technology transfer, quality, digital capability, and manufacturing performance, helping translate complex technical and business priorities into reliable execution.
  
  
You will lead a highly capable team while owning the continuous improvement agenda for DNA Manufacturing, using operational data, structured problem solving, and cross-functional leadership to identify risks, unlock capacity, strengthen processes, and deliver sustainable improvements.
  
  
As a member of the DNA Leadership Team, you will influence priorities beyond your immediate function, solve complex and ambiguous challenges across organizational boundaries, and help build the manufacturing capabilities, culture, and digital ways of working needed for the next stage of Moderna’s operations.
  
  
**Here’s What You’ll Do**

* Lead, develop, and coach a team of Specialists and Senior Specialists with broad expertise across DNA and Cell Bank manufacturing processes, building a highly capable and adaptable team that can address evolving operational priorities.
* Own and continuously improve the DNA Manufacturing continuous improvement and Operational Excellence program, including the identification, prioritization, execution, and benefits realization of improvement opportunities.
* Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives spanning DNA Manufacturing and partner organizations, establishing clear objectives, governance, execution plans, decision-making mechanisms, and accountability for delivery.
* Own the strategy and execution of manufacturing change controls associated with area improvements, ensuring changes are effectively planned, assessed, implemented, embedded, and sustained within manufacturing operations.
* Provide manufacturing leadership and execution support for technology transfers, serving as the Manufacturing representative, coordinating manufacturing readiness activities, and providing project management across cross-functional teams to enable successful transfer and execution.
* Lead the use of operational data, performance indicators, manufacturing trends, and operational insights to proactively identify emerging risks, improvement opportunities, capacity constraints, and priorities for DNA Operations.
* Establish and continuously evolve effective operational performance management mechanisms, including dashboards, routine performance reviews, action tracking, and escalation processes for emerging issues.
* Serve as a GMP leader and manufacturing subject matter expert, providing support for investigations, operational events, risk assessments, change implementation, and other quality system activities as required.
* Partner closely with Manufacturing Science & Technology (MSAT), Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Digital, CMC Development, Planning, and other stakeholders to integrate technical, quality, supply, and business priorities into effective manufacturing execution.
* Support the organization’s ongoing state of inspection readiness, ensuring the team, processes, documentation, change activity, and improvements within the role’s scope are prepared to effectively support regulatory inspections.
* Build organizational capability in continuous improvement, structured problem solving, project execution, data-driven decision making, and change management, strengthening the organization’s ability to respond effectively to evolving manufacturing needs.
* Serve as a member of the DNA Leadership Team, contributing to strategy, organizational priorities, operational performance, workforce engagement, and the resolution of issues affecting the broader DNA Operations organization.
* Foster a positive, collaborative, accountable, and inclusive working culture across DNA Manufacturing, acting as a visible leader and role model while supporting the overall performance and well-being of the organization.
* Act as a trusted advisor and problem solver for DNA Operations leadership, proactively identifying opportunities and taking ownership of complex or ambiguous challenges that cross traditional functional and organizational boundaries.
* Work with Digital and cross-functional partners to explore how Generative AI and other advanced digital tools can strengthen operational insights, structured problem solving, knowledge access, performance management, and decision making, while operating within appropriate manufacturing, quality, and data-governance requirements.
* Drive success through the team’s ability to execute complex initiatives, deliver sustainable improvements, effectively manage change, enable successful technology transfers, use data proactively to identify opportunities and risks, and continuously strengthen the capability and overall performance of DNA Manufacturing.

**The key Moderna Mindsets you’ll need to succeed in the role:**

* “We act with dynamic range, driving strategy and execution at the same time at every step.”
* “We digitize everywhere possible using the power of code to maximize our impact on patients.”

**Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, manufacturing, or another relevant technical discipline or an equivalent combination of education and relevant industry experience.
* Demonstrated experience in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, technical operations, manufacturing sciences, operational excellence, or a related environment.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop people, including creating clarity, setting priorities, coaching performance, and building organizational capability.
* Proven ability to influence and lead effectively within a complex matrix organization, including situations where successful execution requires alignment of stakeholders outside the individual's direct authority.
* Demonstrated ownership and successful execution of complex, cross-functional projects or programs, from problem definition and strategy through implementation and sustained results.
* Experience with GMP manufacturing and quality systems, including change control and other mechanisms used to implement and sustain changes in a regulated environment.
* Experience supporting technology transfer, manufacturing readiness, process implementation, or other cross-functional technical programs.
* Strong understanding of continuous improvement and operational excellence principles, with demonstrated ability to translate them into measurable improvements in manufacturing performance.
* Demonstrated ability to use data, trends, and performance indicators to identify problems, establish priorities, and drive decisions and improvement.
* Strong communication, stakeholder management, and organizational leadership skills, with the ability to communicate effectively from the manufacturing floor through senior leadership.
* Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity, connect technical and business considerations, and take ownership of problems that do not fit neatly within traditional functional boundaries.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and inspection readiness activities preferred.

**Schedule:**
Monday–Friday; flexibility may be required to support critical manufacturing activities, technology transfers, regulatory inspections, or significant operational events.
  
  
**Our Working Model**
As we build our company, we have always believed an in-person culture is critical to our success. Moderna champions the significant benefits of in-office collaboration by embracing a 70/30 work model.
  
  
This 70% in-office structure helps to foster a culture rich in innovation, teamwork, and direct mentorship. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.
  
  
Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.
  
  
**Pay & Benefits**
**At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work.**
**That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.**

* Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
* A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
* Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
* Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
* Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
* Location-specific perks and extras

The salary range for this role is $130,800.00 - $209,400.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance.
  
  
**About Moderna**
Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.
  
  
By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.
  
  
We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.
  
  
If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities.
  
  
**Equal Opportunities**
Moderna is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry or citizenship, ethnicity, disability, military or protected veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital or familial status, or any other personal characteristic protected under applicable law. Moderna is a place where everyone can grow. If you meet the Basic Qualifications for the role and you would be excited to contribute to our mission every day, please apply!
  
  
Moderna is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. We consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.
  
  
**Accommodations**
We’re focused on attracting, retaining, developing, and advancing our employees. By cultivating a workplace that values diverse experiences, backgrounds, and ideas, we create an environment where every employee can contribute their best.

With revenue of more than $9 billion in FY24 and approximately 24,000 people globally, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible™. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and Twitter (X).
  
  
**Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations**
The Camas Wafer Fab is a growing 150mm, high‑volume, 24x7 manufacturing facility producing leading‑edge precision ICs in support of ADI’s diversified semiconductor business.
  
  
Reporting to the Wafer Fab General Manager, the
**Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations**
will lead our ~300‑employee Production organization—including Production Managers, Supervisors, Trainers, 5S & Continuous Improvement, New Product Technicians, Leads, and Operators—who execute day‑to‑day manufacturing, testing, and shipping of a broad product portfolio as the fab continues to ramp, expand, and modernize a facility with over 25 years of operational history.
  
  
Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.
  
  
**Job Duties**
The Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations is a senior operations leader responsible for translating site strategy into strong operational execution. Responsibilities are aligned to three core competency areas:
  
  
**Operational & Strategic Execution**

* Translate site and enterprise manufacturing strategies into actionable operational plans for the Production organization, aligned with objectives for safety, quality, productivity, cost, talent development, and sustainability.
* Lead the execution of production improvement roadmaps, supporting longer‑term digital transformation, automation, and modernization initiatives defined at the site level.
* Drive adoption of data‑driven and AI‑enabled decision making within production operations, leveraging analytics, automation, and machine‑learning‑based insights to improve daily execution and performance stability.
* Support change management efforts associated with new technologies, digital tools, demand shifts, and new product introductions, ensuring disciplined adoption on the production floor.
* Share and apply best‑known methods from across ADI’s manufacturing network to continuously elevate production performance.

**Operational Excellence**

* Maintain a safe and healthy work environment by enforcing organizational standards, adhering to 5S principles, and complying with ADI policies, legal requirements, and regulatory standards.
* Own day‑to‑day production quality performance, applying a zero‑defect mindset using traditional quality methodologies (8D, 5‑Why, SPC) and AI‑assisted defect detection, yield analysis, and trend identification.
* Lead execution of production plans that deliver short‑term tactical results while driving continuous improvement across Safety, Quality, Productivity, Cost, and Efficiency metrics.
* Utilize predictive and prescriptive analytics, where applicable, to anticipate equipment issues, process drift, capacity constraints, and safety risks before they impact performance.
* Provide clear tactical direction through written reports, dashboards, presentations, daily operational reviews, all‑hands meetings, and shift‑level stand‑ups, ensuring decisions are grounded in accurate, timely data.
* Lead capacity modeling, scenario analysis, and demand response activities within the production organization, partnering with site leadership on longer‑range planning.
* Partner closely with Supply Chain to optimize wafer starts, cycle time, and scheduling, balancing customer demand with fab constraints and operational risk.
* Participate in internal and external audits to ensure compliance, business continuity, and continuous improvement, including adherence to ADI’s responsible and ethical use of AI in manufacturing operations.
* Support the development and ramp of new products and non‑standard fabrication requirements while maintaining safe, stable, and predictable production output.
* Ensure effective cross‑training programs and skills matrices are in place, leveraging digital tools to improve workforce flexibility and readiness.

**Effective Team Leadership**

* Lead recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and training efforts for the Production organization, aligning staffing plans with quarterly and longer‑range production needs.
* Foster a culture of engagement, accountability, and continuous improvement through proactive communication, coaching, and visible leadership presence across all shifts.
* Develop production supervisors and frontline leaders capable of operating in an increasingly digital, automated, and data‑driven manufacturing environment.
* Execute effective performance management processes to improve team continuity, leadership capability, and operational results.
* Partner with Human Resources to support competency development, technical capability building, and training plans aligned with future manufacturing needs.
* Ensure alignment with ADI Enterprise Excellence Guiding Principles, emphasizing safety, quality, operational rigor, and responsible innovation.

**SCHEDULE**
This is an exempt role, working on‑site in Camas, Washington, primarily Monday through Friday, supporting a 24x7 continuous operation.
  
  
Occasional night or weekend hours are required to support operational needs.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or a related field required; technical or engineering degree strongly preferred.
* 8+ years of leadership experience in high‑volume wafer fabrication or advanced manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated success leading large production teams through supervisors and frontline leaders.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with proven effectiveness in a data‑driven, metrics‑based operating environment.
* Solid working knowledge of manufacturing and business systems (ERP/MRP, MES, dispatching, capacity planning, Microsoft Office).
* Demonstrated ability to apply analytics, digital tools, and emerging AI/ML capabilities to improve safety, quality, productivity, and cost performance.
* Strong problem‑solving skills, operational discipline, and passion for continuous improvement.

**Bring more to life.**
Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology?
  
  
At Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.
  
  
You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.
  
  
At Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, we know time is the most critical facet in the laboratory today:  time to get life-saving therapies to patients faster; reclaiming time by automating tedious manual workflows; and saving time spent addressing erroneous or complex results.
  
  
We are partners in time and accelerate answers to critical questions through the power of automation. We develop innovations for scientists by scientists, with many of our 3,300+ global colleagues coming from the laboratory.
  
  
It’s all part of our time-tested approach to bringing meaningful innovations at the speed of life since 1935. And we’re just beginning. Working together, let’s put our time and talents together to advance human health for tomorrow.
  
  
Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.
  
  
The
**Senior Manager - Global New Product Introduction (NPI)**
- Systems Hardware is responsible for leading Manufacturing Engineering and Operations readiness for hardware- and systems-based product development programs across Beckman Coulter Life Sciences' global manufacturing network. This leader serves as the critical bridge between R&D, Product Management, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Service, and Manufacturing Operations to ensure successful design transfer, manufacturing scale-up, and on-time commercialization of complex life science instrumentation.
  
  
This position reports to the Director, Manufacturing Engineering and is part of the Global Manufacturing Engineering & Innovation organization located in Indianapolis, Indiana. This will be an on-site role with global collaboration across U.S., China, and Europe BEC LS manufacturing and development locations as required.
  
  
**In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To**

* Lead Manufacturing Engineering engagement from product concept through commercialization for hardware and instrument platforms, ensuring safety, quality, delivery, cost, supply continuity, reliability, capacity, and launch objectives are achieved.
* Lead governance for the global hardware NPI portfolio, including milestones, resource prioritization, capital plans, risk management, escalation paths, launch metrics, executive reviews, and post-launch stabilization.
* Partner with the Director, Manufacturing Engineering to develop and deploy global NPI and manufacturing engineering strategies aligned with business growth, product roadmaps, manufacturing footprint, capacity, lifecycle, and innovation priorities.
* Ensure robust design transfer and manufacturing readiness across U.S., China, and Europe locations, including manufacturing requirements, process development, equipment and tooling, pilot builds, test methods, documentation, process validation, production ramp, and issue closure.
* Drive Design for Manufacturing, Assembly, Test, Service, Reliability, and Cost in partnership with R&D and other functions, using the Danaher Business System, standard work, visual management, value stream mapping, daily management, kaizen, and structured problem solving.
* Lead selected global manufacturing excellence initiatives involving engineering standards, process capability, automation, digital manufacturing, manufacturing technology, test strategy, productivity, value engineering, and continuous cost improvement.
* Lead and develop managers, engineers, and technical project leaders across a global matrix; strengthen accountability, technical capability, talent reviews, succession planning, leadership development, inclusion, and mobility across global and site teams.

**The Essential Requirements Of The Job Include**

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Biomedical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Systems, or a closely related engineering discipline.
* Typically 10+ years of progressive experience across engineering, manufacturing, operations, product development, and/or new product introduction.
* At least 5 years of people leadership experience, with demonstrated ability to lead managers, engineers, or technical project leaders across locations or in a global matrix. Working knowledge of FDA, ISO, quality-system, design-control, risk-management, verification and validation, change-control, traceability, process-validation, and product-lifecycle requirements.
* Demonstrated success launching complex electromechanical, software-enabled, diagnostic, medical device, or life science instrumentation products in regulated manufacturing environments.
* Deep experience with design transfer, industrialization, manufacturing readiness, process development and validation, manufacturing test, tooling and equipment, supplier readiness, ramp, and lifecycle support.
* Proven ability to translate business and product strategy into engineering priorities, operating mechanisms, investment recommendations, and measurable results. Experience leading portfolio governance, resource prioritization, capital planning, risk reviews, and cross-functional executive decision-making.

**It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:**

* Master’s degree in engineering, an MBA, PMP certification, Lean Six Sigma certification, or comparable advanced development.
* Experience with flow cytometry, centrifugation, liquid handling, particle characterization, genomics, bioprocessing, or comparable scientific instrumentation platforms.
* Experience leading global engineering transformation, automation, digital manufacturing, connected equipment, manufacturing data systems, or advanced analytics initiatives.
* Experience with site transfers, localization, manufacturing footprint changes, contract manufacturers, supplier development, acquisition integration, or rapid capacity expansion.

Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, a Danaher operating company, offers a broad array of comprehensive, competitive benefit programs that add value to our lives. Whether it’s a health care program or paid time off, our programs contribute to life beyond the job. Check out our benefits at Danaher Benefits Info.
  
  
We offer comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance and 401(k) to eligible employees.
  
  
Join our winning team today. Together, we’ll accelerate the real-life impact of tomorrow’s science and technology. We partner with customers across the globe to help them solve their most complex challenges, architecting solutions that bring the power of science to life.
  
  
For more information, visit www.danaher.com.
